title.zh: 卷八十七 列傳第三十七: 裴炎 劉禕之 魏玄同 李昭德
title.en: Volume 87 Biographies 37: Pei Yan, Liu Yizhi, Wei Xuantong, Li Zhaode
title.raw: 卷八十七 列傳第三十七: 裴炎 劉禕之 魏玄同 李昭德 Volume 87 Biographies 37: Pei Yan, Liu Yizhi, Wei Xuantong, Li Zhaode

sentences.zh: 裴炎劉禕之魏玄同李昭德

translations.literal: Pei Yan, Liu Yizhi, Wei Xuantong, Li Zhaode
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yan, Liu Yizhi, Wei Xuantong, and Li Zhaode

sentences.zh: 裴炎，絳州聞喜人也。

translations.literal: Pei Yan was a man of Wenxi in Jiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yan was a native of Wenxi in Jiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少補弘文生，每遇休假，諸生多出遊，炎獨不廢業。

translations.literal: In his youth he entered the Hongwen Academy as a student; whenever there were holidays, the other students mostly went out on excursions, but Yan alone did not neglect his studies.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he enrolled in the Hongwen Academy; on holidays, when most students went out for pleasure, Yan alone kept to his studies.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，有司將薦舉，辭以學未篤而止。

translations.literal: After more than a year, the authorities were about to recommend him, but he declined on the grounds that his learning was not yet solid, and the matter stopped there.
translations.idiomatic: After a year or more, the authorities prepared to nominate him, but he declined, saying his scholarship was not yet mature enough.

sentences.zh: 在館垂十載，尤曉《春秋左氏傳》及《漢書》。

translations.literal: He remained at the academy for nearly ten years and was especially versed in the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals and the Book of Han.
translations.idiomatic: He spent nearly ten years in the academy and became especially expert in the Zuo Commentary and the Book of Han.

sentences.zh: 擢明經第，尋為濮州司倉參軍。

translations.literal: He passed the Mingjing examination and soon became a staff officer in the revenue office of Pu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the Mingjing examination and was soon appointed revenue staff officer at Pu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 累曆兵部侍郎、中書門下平章事、侍中、中書令。

translations.literal: He successively served as vice minister of war, joint holder of the office of Grand Councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery, Palace Attendant, and Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the posts of vice minister of war, grand councilor, palace attendant, and director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 永淳元年，高宗幸東都，留太子哲守京師，命炎與劉仁軌、薛元超為輔。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongchun, Gaozong visited the Eastern Capital, left Crown Prince Zhe to guard the capital, and ordered Yan to assist him together with Liu Rengui and Xue Yuanchao.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongchun, Gaozong went to the Eastern Capital, left Crown Prince Zhe in Chang'an, and ordered Yan, Liu Rengui, and Xue Yuanchao to assist him.

sentences.zh: 明年，高宗不豫，炎從太子赴東都侍疾。

translations.literal: The next year Gaozong fell ill; Yan followed the crown prince to the Eastern Capital to attend him in his illness.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, when Gaozong fell ill, Yan followed the crown prince east to attend him.

sentences.zh: 十一月，高宗疾篤，命太子監國，炎奉詔與黃門侍郎劉齊賢、中書侍郎郭正一並於東宮平章事。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Gaozong's illness became critical; the crown prince was ordered to supervise the state; Yan received an edict to serve with Vice Director of the Yellow Gate Liu Qixian and Vice Director of the Secretariat Guo Zhengyi jointly as grand councilors at the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, as Gaozong's illness turned critical, the crown prince was ordered to supervise the realm. Yan received an edict to deliberate on state affairs at the Eastern Palace with Liu Qixian and Guo Zhengyi.

sentences.zh: 十二月丁巳，高宗崩，太子即位。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on dingsi, Gaozong died and the crown prince ascended the throne.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on dingsi, Gaozong died and the crown prince took the throne.

sentences.zh: 未聽政，宰臣奏議，天後降令於門下施行。

translations.literal: Before attending to government, when the chief ministers deliberated and submitted proposals, the Empress Dowager issued orders from the Chancellery for implementation.
translations.idiomatic: Before he took up rule, when the chief ministers submitted proposals, the Empress Dowager issued orders through the Chancellery for their implementation.

sentences.zh: 中宗既立，欲以後父韋玄貞為侍中，又欲與乳母子五品，炎固爭以為不可。

translations.literal: After Zhongzong had taken the throne, he wished to make his father-in-law Wei Xuanzhen palace attendant and also to grant fifth rank to the sons of his wet nurse; Yan stubbornly argued that this could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhongzong had ascended, he wished to make his father-in-law Wei Xuanzhen palace attendant and grant fifth rank to his wet nurse's sons; Yan firmly argued that this could not be allowed.

sentences.zh: 中宗不悅，謂左右曰：“我讓國與玄貞豈不得，何為惜侍中耶？”

translations.literal: Zhongzong was displeased and said to those around him: "If I yield the realm to Xuanzhen, would that not be permitted—why begrudge the post of palace attendant?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong was displeased and told his attendants: "If I yield the empire to Xuanzhen, would that not be allowed—why quibble over the post of palace attendant?"

sentences.zh: 炎懼，乃與則天定策廢立。

translations.literal: Yan feared this and therefore joined Zetian in plotting deposition and enthronement.
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed, Yan joined Zetian in plotting to depose and enthrone.

sentences.zh: 炎與中書侍郎劉禕之、羽林將軍程務挺、張虔勖等勒兵入內，宣太后令，扶帝下殿。

translations.literal: Yan, together with Vice Director of the Secretariat Liu Yizhi, Yulin General Cheng Wuting, Zhang Qianxu, and others, led troops into the inner palace, proclaimed the Empress Dowager's order, and helped the emperor down from the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Yan, Liu Yizhi, Cheng Wuting, Zhang Qianxu, and others led troops into the palace, proclaimed the Empress Dowager's order, and brought the emperor down from the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：“我有何罪？”

translations.literal: The emperor said: "What crime have I committed?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "What crime have I committed?"

sentences.zh: 太后報曰：“汝若將天下與韋玄貞，何得無罪！”

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager replied: "If you were to give the realm to Wei Xuanzhen, how could you be without guilt!"
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager replied: "If you were to give the empire to Wei Xuanzhen, how could you be guiltless!"

sentences.zh: 乃廢中宗為盧陵王，立豫王旦為帝。

translations.literal: They then deposed Zhongzong as Prince of Luling and enthroned Prince of Yu Dan as emperor.
translations.idiomatic: They deposed Zhongzong as Prince of Luling and enthroned Prince of Yu Dan as emperor.

sentences.zh: 炎以定策功，封河東縣侯。

translations.literal: For his merit in settling the succession, Yan was enfeoffed as Marquis of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: For his role in fixing the succession, Yan was enfeoffed Marquis of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 太后臨朝，天授初，又降豫王為皇嗣。

translations.literal: When the Empress Dowager held court, at the beginning of the Tianshou era she again demoted the Prince of Yu to heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: After the Empress Dowager took power, in the early Tianshou period she demoted the Prince of Yu to heir apparent once more.

sentences.zh: 時太后侄武承嗣請立武氏七廟及追王父祖，太后將許之。

translations.literal: At that time the Empress Dowager's nephew Wu Chengsi requested the establishment of seven ancestral temples for the Wu clan and posthumous ennoblement of his father and grandfather as kings; the Empress Dowager was about to grant it.
translations.idiomatic: At that time her nephew Wu Chengsi asked to establish seven ancestral temples for the Wu house and to ennoble his forefathers posthumously as kings, and the Empress Dowager was on the verge of approving.

sentences.zh: 炎進諫曰：“皇太后天下之母，聖德臨朝，當存至公，不宜追王祖禰，以示自私。

translations.literal: Yan remonstrated, saying: "The Empress Dowager is mother of the realm; with her sagely virtue holding court, she should preserve utmost impartiality and ought not to ennoble the Wu ancestors, which would show selfishness.
translations.idiomatic: Yan remonstrated: "Your Majesty is mother of the empire. In governing with sagely virtue you should remain utterly impartial. You ought not to ennoble the Wu ancestors, for that would look like self-interest.

sentences.zh: 且獨不見呂氏之敗乎？

translations.literal: Moreover, have you alone not seen the ruin of the Lü clan?
translations.idiomatic: Have you not seen how the Lü clan came to ruin?

sentences.zh: 臣恐後之視今，亦猶今之視昔。”

translations.literal: Your subject fears that those who come after will view the present as we now view the past."
translations.idiomatic: I fear posterity will judge our age as we now judge earlier times."

sentences.zh: 太后曰：“呂氏之王，權在生人；

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager said: "When the Lü were made kings, power lay with the living;
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager replied: "The Lü were made kings while they still held living power.

sentences.zh: 今者追尊，事歸前代。

translations.literal: what is sought now is posthumous honor, a matter belonging to a former age.
translations.idiomatic: What we seek now is posthumous honor alone, a matter of the past.

sentences.zh: 存歿殊跡，豈可同日而言？”

translations.literal: The living and the dead follow different paths—how can they be spoken of on the same day?"
translations.idiomatic: The living and the dead are not the same case. How can the two be compared?"

sentences.zh: 炎曰：“蔓草難圖，漸不可長。

translations.literal: Yan said: "Creeping weeds are hard to uproot; what grows gradually must not be allowed to lengthen.
translations.idiomatic: Yan said: "Weeds spread until they are hard to clear. What grows by degrees must not be indulged.

sentences.zh: 殷鑒未遠，當絕其源。”

translations.literal: The lesson of the recent past is not far off; the source should be cut off."
translations.idiomatic: The warning of the recent past is still close at hand. Cut it off at the root."

sentences.zh: 太后不悅而止。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager was displeased and stopped the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager took offense and dropped the proposal.

sentences.zh: 時韓王元嘉、魯王靈夔等皆皇屬之近，承嗣與從父弟三思屢勸太后因事誅之，以絕宗室之望。

translations.literal: At that time the Prince of Han, Yuanjia, the Prince of Lu, Lingqi, and others were all close imperial kin; Chengsi and his cousin Wu Sansi repeatedly urged the Empress Dowager to have them executed on some pretext, so as to cut off the hopes of the imperial house.
translations.idiomatic: The Princes of Han and Lu, Yuanjia and Lingqi, were close members of the imperial clan. Chengsi and his cousin Sansi repeatedly urged the Empress Dowager to find grounds to execute them and thereby extinguish the hopes of the imperial house.

sentences.zh: 劉禕之、韋仁約並懷畏憚，唯唯無言，炎獨固爭，以為不可，承嗣深憾之。

translations.literal: Liu Yizhi and Wei Renyue both harbored fear and kept silent in assent; Yan alone argued firmly that it could not be done, and Chengsi deeply resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yizhi and Wei Renyue were afraid and said nothing. Yan alone argued firmly that it must not be done, and Chengsi bore him a deep grudge.

sentences.zh: 文明元年，官名改易，炎為內史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wenming, when official titles were changed, Yan became Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wenming, when titles were reorganized, Yan became Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 秋，徐敬業構逆，太后召炎議事。

translations.literal: In autumn Xu Jingye raised rebellion; the Empress Dowager summoned Yan to discuss affairs.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Xu Jingye rebelled, and the Empress Dowager summoned Yan to counsel her.

sentences.zh: 炎奏曰：“皇帝年長，未俾親政，乃致猾豎有詞。

translations.literal: Yan memorialized, saying: "The Emperor is already grown, yet has not been allowed to rule in person, and so crafty villains have grounds to speak.
translations.idiomatic: Yan submitted: "The Emperor is already grown, yet he has not been allowed to rule in person. That is why scheming villains have something to say.

sentences.zh: 若太后返政，則此賊不討而解矣。”

translations.literal: If the Empress Dowager returns power, then this rebel will dissolve without being punished."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty returns power to him, this rebel will collapse without a fight."

sentences.zh: 御史崔察聞而上言，曰：“裴炎伏事先朝，二十餘載，受遺顧托，大權在己，若無異圖，何故請太后歸政？”

translations.literal: The censor Cui Cha heard of it and submitted, saying: "Pei Yan served the former court for more than twenty years, received the dying charge and trust, and held great power in his own hands; if he had no other design, why did he ask the Empress Dowager to return power?"
translations.idiomatic: Censor Cui Cha heard of this and reported: "Pei Yan served the late emperor for more than twenty years, received his deathbed trust, and held supreme power. If he harbored no ulterior design, why would he ask the Empress Dowager to yield power?"

sentences.zh: 乃命御史大夫騫味道、御史魚承曄鞫之。

translations.literal: She then ordered the Censor-in-Chief Qian Weidao and the censor Yu Chengye to investigate him.
translations.idiomatic: She ordered Censor-in-Chief Qian Weidao and Censor Yu Chengye to interrogate him.

sentences.zh: 鳳閣侍郎胡元範奏曰：“炎社稷忠臣，有功於國，悉心奉上，天下所知，臣明其不反。”

translations.literal: The Vice Director of the Phoenix Pavilion Hu Yuanfan memorialized, saying: "Yan is a loyal minister of the altars of state, has merit toward the realm, and devotes himself to serving above; all under Heaven know it. Your subject knows clearly that he does not rebel."
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Hu Yuanfan memorialized: "Yan is a loyal servant of the state who has served the throne with devotion and earned merit for the realm. All the world knows this. I am certain he is not a rebel."

sentences.zh: 右衛大將軍程務挺密表申理之，文武之間證炎不反者甚眾，太后皆不納。

translations.literal: The General of the Right Guards Cheng Wuting submitted a secret memorial pleading his case; among civil and military officials very many testified that Yan did not rebel, but the Empress Dowager accepted none of it.
translations.idiomatic: General Cheng Wuting sent a secret memorial in his defense. Many officials, civil and military, testified that Yan was no rebel, but the Empress Dowager would hear none of it.

sentences.zh: 光宅元年十月，斬炎於都亭驛之前街。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the first year of Guangzhai, Yan was beheaded in the street before the Duting Post Station.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the first year of Guangzhai, Yan was beheaded in the street before the Duting courier station.

sentences.zh: 炎初被擒，左右勸炎遜詞於使者，炎歎曰：“宰相下獄，焉有更全之理！”

translations.literal: When Yan was first seized, those around him urged him to use humble words with the envoys; Yan sighed and said: "When a chief minister is cast into prison, how can there be any further hope of coming out whole!"
translations.idiomatic: When Yan was first arrested, his attendants urged him to speak humbly to the investigators. He sighed and said: "When a chief minister is thrown into prison, what hope is there of coming out whole?"

sentences.zh: 竟無折節。

translations.literal: In the end he never bent his integrity.
translations.idiomatic: He never humbled himself to the end.

sentences.zh: 及籍沒其家，乃無儋石之蓄。

translations.literal: When his household goods were inventoried and confiscated, there was not even a dan or shi of stored wealth.
translations.idiomatic: When his property was confiscated, there was scarcely enough grain to fill a single jar.

sentences.zh: 胡元範，申州義陽人，坐救炎流死瓊州。

translations.literal: Hu Yuanfan, a native of Yiyang in Shen Prefecture, was exiled to Qiong Prefecture and died there for having pleaded for Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Yuanfan of Yiyang in Shen Prefecture was exiled to Qiong Prefecture, where he died for having defended Yan.

sentences.zh: 程務挺伏法，納言劉齊賢貶吉州長史，吏部侍郎郭待舉貶岳州刺史，皆坐救炎之罪也。

translations.literal: Cheng Wuting was executed by law; the Counselor Liu Qixian was demoted to chief administrator of Ji Prefecture; the vice minister of personnel Guo Daiju was demoted to prefect of Yue Prefecture—all for the crime of having pleaded for Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Wuting was executed. Counselor Liu Qixian was demoted to chief administrator of Ji Prefecture, and Vice Minister of Personnel Guo Daiju to prefect of Yue Prefecture—all punished for having tried to save Yan.

sentences.zh: 先是，開耀元年十月，定襄道行軍大總管裴行儉獻定襄所獲俘囚，除曲赦外，斬阿史那伏念，溫傅等五十四人於都市。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the tenth month of the first year of Kaiyao, the Commander-in-Chief on campaign along the Dingxiang route Pei Xingjian presented captives taken at Dingxiang; apart from a partial amnesty, Ashina Funician, Wen Fu, and fifty-four others were beheaded in the market of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the tenth month of the first year of Kaiyao, Commander-in-Chief Pei Xingjian of the Dingxiang campaign presented the captives taken there. Aside from those covered by a partial amnesty, Ashina Funician, Wen Fu, and fifty-four others were beheaded in the capital market.

sentences.zh: 初，行儉討伐之時，許伏念以不死，伏念乃降。

translations.literal: At first, when Xingjian was campaigning, he promised Funician that he would not be put to death, and so Funician surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: During the campaign Xingjian had promised Funician his life, and on that promise Funician had surrendered.

sentences.zh: 時炎害行儉之功，奏云：“伏念是程務挺、張虔勖逼逐於營，又磧北回紇南向逼之，窘急而降。”

translations.literal: At that time Yan, jealous of Xingjian's merit, memorialized, saying: "Funician was driven from camp by Cheng Wuting and Zhang Qianxu, and was also pressed from the south by the Uyghurs north of the desert; he surrendered in distress."
translations.idiomatic: Yan, jealous of Xingjian's achievement, memorialized that Funician had been driven from camp by Cheng Wuting and Zhang Qianxu and pressed from the north by the Uyghurs, and had surrendered only in desperation."

sentences.zh: 乃殺之。

translations.literal: He was then killed.
translations.idiomatic: On that basis he was executed.

sentences.zh: 行儉歎曰：“渾、浚之事，古今恥之。

translations.literal: Xingjian sighed and said: "The affairs of Hun and Jun have been a shame in every age.
translations.idiomatic: Xingjian sighed: "What Hun and Jun did has been a disgrace in every age.

sentences.zh: 但恐殺降之後，無復來者。”

translations.literal: I only fear that after killing those who surrender, there will be no one who comes again."
translations.idiomatic: I fear that after we kill men who have surrendered, no one will ever come again."

sentences.zh: 行儉因此稱疾不出。

translations.literal: Because of this Xingjian pleaded illness and did not go out.
translations.idiomatic: After this Xingjian pleaded illness and withdrew from office.

sentences.zh: 炎致國家負義而殺降，妒能害功，構成陰禍，其敗也宜哉！

translations.literal: Yan caused the state to break faith and kill those who surrendered, envied ability and harmed merit, and brought about hidden calamity—was it not fitting that he should fall!
translations.idiomatic: Yan made the state break faith by killing surrendered enemies, envied talent and harmed merit, and brought hidden ruin upon himself. Small wonder he came to ruin!

sentences.zh: 睿宗踐祚，下製曰：“飾終追遠，斯乃舊章；

translations.literal: When Emperor Ruizong took the throne, he issued an edict, saying: "Adorning the end and honoring the distant—this is the old rule;
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ruizong ascended the throne, he issued an edict: "To honor the dead and remember the distant past is an ancient rule.

sentences.zh: 表德旌賢，有光恒策。

translations.literal: displaying virtue and commending the worthy brings glory to enduring policy.
translations.idiomatic: To display virtue and commend the worthy lends luster to enduring policy.

sentences.zh: 故中書令裴炎，含弘稟粹，履信居貞，望重國華，才稱人秀。

translations.literal: The late Director of the Secretariat Pei Yan embraced breadth and received purity, kept faith and held to constancy, stood heavy in the nation's glory, and his talent matched the finest of men.
translations.idiomatic: The late Director of the Secretariat Pei Yan was broad in spirit and pure in nature, steadfast in faith and firm in integrity, eminent in the nation's esteem, and outstanding in talent.

sentences.zh: 唯幾成務，績宣於代工；

translations.literal: Perceiving the subtle, he accomplished affairs; his achievements were proclaimed in service to the regent.
translations.idiomatic: Perceiving what was subtle, he carried out the work of state and won merit in service to the regent.

sentences.zh: 偶居無猜，義深於奉上。

translations.literal: By chance he dwelt without suspicion, and his righteousness toward serving above ran deep.
translations.idiomatic: He served without suspicion and with deep loyalty to the throne.

sentences.zh: 文明之際，王室多虞，保乂朕躬，實著誠節。

translations.literal: At the time of Wenming the royal house had many anxieties; in protecting and comforting Our person he truly showed sincere integrity.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wenming period, when the royal house faced many perils, he protected and comforted Our person and showed true loyalty.

sentences.zh: 而危疑起釁，倉卒羅災，歲月屢遷，丘封莫樹。

translations.literal: Yet doubt and peril gave rise to strife; in haste disaster fell upon him; years have repeatedly passed, and no mound has been raised for his tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Yet suspicion and peril brought strife, and disaster struck him in haste. Years have passed, and no tomb mound has yet been raised.

sentences.zh: 永言先正，感悼良多。

translations.literal: Ever speaking of this former upright man, Our grief and lament are many.
translations.idiomatic: Speaking always of this upright man of old, We feel deep grief and regret.

sentences.zh: 宜追賁於九原，俾增榮於萬古。

translations.literal: He should be posthumously honored in the Nine Plains and have glory added for ten thousand ages.
translations.idiomatic: Let him be honored in the realm of the dead and given glory for ten thousand ages.

sentences.zh: 可贈益州大都督。”

translations.literal: He may be posthumously granted the title of Grand Protector General of Yi Prefecture."
translations.idiomatic: He is posthumously to be made Grand Protector General of Yi Prefecture."

sentences.zh: 炎長子彥先，後為太子舍人；

translations.literal: Yan's eldest son Yanzian later became an attendant of the Heir Apparent;
translations.idiomatic: Yan's eldest son Yanzian later served as attendant to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 從子伷先，後為工部尚書。

translations.literal: his nephew's son Youxian later became minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew's son Youxian later became minister of works.

sentences.zh: 劉禕之，常州晉陵人也。

translations.literal: Liu Yizhi was a man of Jinling in Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yizhi was a native of Jinling in Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖興宗，陳鄱陽王諮議參軍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xingzong served as consultation and planning staff officer to the Prince of Poyang of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xingzong served as staff advisor to the Prince of Poyang of Chen.

sentences.zh: 父子翼，善吟諷，有學行。

translations.literal: His father Ziyi was skilled at chanting and recitation and possessed learning and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ziyi was skilled at chanting and recitation and was a man of learning and integrity.

sentences.zh: 隋大業初，歷秘書監，河東柳顧言甚重之。

translations.literal: In the early Daye period of Sui he served as Director of the Secretariat; Liu Guyan of Hedong greatly valued him.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Daye era of Sui he served as Director of the Secretariat, and Liu Guyan of Hedong held him in high esteem.

sentences.zh: 性不容非，朋僚有短，面折之。

translations.literal: By nature he would not tolerate wrongdoing; when colleagues had faults, he reproved them to their faces.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he would not tolerate wrongdoing; when colleagues erred, he reproved them to their faces.

sentences.zh: 友人李伯藥常稱曰：“劉四雖復罵人，人都不恨。”

translations.literal: His friend Li Boyao often said: "Even when Liu the Fourth scolds people, no one resents him."
translations.idiomatic: His friend Li Boyao often said: "Even when Liu the Fourth scolds people, no one bears resentment."

sentences.zh: 貞觀元年，詔追入京，以母老固辭，太宗許其終養。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenguan, an edict summoned him to the capital; citing his aged mother, he firmly declined, and Taizong permitted him to care for her to the end.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhenguan, an edict summoned him to the capital; citing his aged mother, he firmly declined, and Taizong allowed him to care for her until her death.

sentences.zh: 江南大使李襲譽嘉其至孝，恒以米帛賚之，因上表旌其門閭，改所居為孝慈里。

translations.literal: The Jiangnan commissioner Li Xiyu admired his utmost filial piety and constantly rewarded him with grain and silk; he therefore submitted a memorial commending his household gate and lane, renaming his residence Filial and Kind Lane.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangnan commissioner Li Xiyu admired his filial devotion and constantly rewarded him with grain and silk; he memorialized to honor his household gate and renamed his residence Filial and Kind Lane.

sentences.zh: 母卒，服竟，征拜吳王府功曹，再遷著作郎、弘文館直學士，預修《晉書》，加朝散大夫。

translations.literal: When his mother died and mourning was complete, he was summoned and appointed steward of the Prince of Wu's household; he was twice transferred to director of writings and academician on duty at the Hongwen Hall, took part in compiling the Book of Jin, and was given the additional rank of Grand Master of the Morning Court.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother died and mourning ended, he was summoned as steward of the Prince of Wu's household, then promoted to director of writings and resident academician of the Hongwen Hall. He helped compile the Book of Jin and was given the additional rank of Grand Master of the Morning Court.

sentences.zh: 永徽初卒，高宗遣使弔贈，給靈輿還鄉。

translations.literal: He died at the beginning of Yonghui; Gaozong sent envoys to mourn and grant posthumous honors and provided a funeral carriage to return his body home.
translations.idiomatic: He died early in the Yonghui era; Gaozong sent envoys to mourn and honor him and provided a funeral carriage to return his body home.

sentences.zh: 有集二十卷。

translations.literal: He left a collected works in twenty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He left collected works in twenty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 禕之少與孟利貞、高智周、郭正一俱以文藻知名，時人號為劉、孟、高、郭。

translations.literal: In his youth Yizhi, together with Meng Lizhen, Gao Zhizhou, and Guo Zhengyi, was famed for literary ornament, and men of the time called them Liu, Meng, Gao, and Guo.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Yizhi, together with Meng Lizhen, Gao Zhizhou, and Guo Zhengyi, was famed for literary talent, and contemporaries called them the Liu, Meng, Gao, and Guo.

sentences.zh: 尋與利貞等同直昭文館。

translations.literal: Soon he and Lizhen and the others served together on duty at the Zhaowen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he and Lizhen served together on duty at the Zhaowen Hall.

sentences.zh: 上元中，遷左史、弘文館直學士，與著作郎元萬頃，左史范履冰、苗楚客，右史周思茂、韓楚賓等皆召入禁中，共撰《列女傳》、《臣軌》、《百僚新誡》、《樂書》，凡千餘卷。

translations.literal: In the Shangyuan era he was promoted to Left Historian and academician on duty at the Hongwen Hall; together with the director of writings Yuan Wanqing, the Left Historians Fan Lübing and Miao Chuke, the Right Historians Zhou Simao and Han Chubin, and others, he was all summoned into the inner palace to compile the Biographies of Exemplary Women, the Tracks of Ministers, the New Admonitions for the Hundred Officials, and the Book of Music—more than a thousand juan in all.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shangyuan era he was promoted to Left Historian and resident academician of the Hongwen Hall. He and Yuan Wanqing, Fan Lübing, Miao Chuke, Zhou Simao, Han Chubin, and others were summoned into the inner palace to compile the Biographies of Exemplary Women, the Tracks of Ministers, the New Admonitions for the Hundred Officials, and the Book of Music—more than a thousand scrolls in all.

sentences.zh: 時又密令參決，以分宰相之權，時人謂之“北門學士”。

translations.literal: At that time they were also secretly ordered to join in decisions, so as to divide the power of the chief ministers; men of the time called them the "North Gate Academicians."
translations.idiomatic: They were also secretly ordered to take part in policy decisions and thereby divide the power of the chief ministers. Contemporaries called them the North Gate Academicians.

sentences.zh: 禕之兄懿之，時為給事中，兄弟並居兩省，論者美之。

translations.literal: Yizhi's elder brother Yizhi was at that time a supervising secretary; the brothers both held posts in the two secretariats, and commentators praised this.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Yizhi was then a supervising secretary. With both brothers serving in the two secretariats, commentators praised the arrangement.

sentences.zh: 儀鳳二年，轉朝議大夫、中書侍郎，兼豫王府司馬，尋加中大夫。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yifeng he was transferred to Gentleman for Court Discussion, vice director of the Secretariat, and concurrently steward of the Prince of Yu's household; soon he was given the additional rank of Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yifeng he became Gentleman for Court Discussion and vice director of the Secretariat, while also serving as steward of the Prince of Yu's household. Soon he was promoted to grand master.

sentences.zh: 禕之有姊在宮中為內職，天后令省榮國夫人之疾，禕之潛伺見之，坐是配流巂州。

translations.literal: Yizhi had an elder sister serving in the palace as an inner attendant; the Heavenly Empress ordered her to visit Lady Rongguo in her illness, and Yizhi secretly watched and saw her; for this he was banished to Xun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhi had an elder sister serving in the palace. When the Empress ordered her to visit Lady Rongguo during an illness, Yizhi secretly went to see her and was banished to Xun Prefecture for it.

sentences.zh: 歷數載，天后表請高宗召還，拜中書舍人。

translations.literal: After several years the Heavenly Empress submitted a memorial asking Emperor Gaozong to recall him, and he was appointed drafting officer of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After several years the Empress memorialized Gaozong to recall him, and he was appointed drafting officer of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 轉相王府司馬，復遷檢校中書侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to steward of the Prince of Xiang's household and again promoted to acting vice director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to steward of the Prince of Xiang's household and later promoted again to acting vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 高宗謂曰：“相王朕之愛子，以卿忠孝之門，藉卿師範，所冀蓬生麻中，不扶自直耳。”

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong said to him: "The Prince of Xiang is Our beloved son; because your house is one of loyalty and filial piety, We rely on you as his teacher and model, hoping that like mugwort growing amid hemp he will stand straight without being propped up."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong told him: "The Prince of Xiang is Our beloved son. Because yours is a house of loyalty and filial piety, We rely on you as his teacher, hoping that, like mugwort growing amid hemp, he will stand straight without propping."

sentences.zh: 禕之居家孝友，甚為士族所稱，每得俸祿，散於親屬，高宗以此重之。

translations.literal: Yizhi was filial and friendly at home and was greatly praised by the gentry; whenever he received salary he distributed it among his kin, and for this Gaozong held him in high regard.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhi was filial and friendly at home and was greatly praised by the gentry. Whenever he received his salary he distributed it among his relatives, and for this Gaozong esteemed him highly.

sentences.zh: 則天臨朝，甚見親委。

translations.literal: When Wu Zetian held court she greatly favored and entrusted him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Zetian took power she favored and trusted him greatly.

sentences.zh: 及豫王立，禕之參預其謀，擢拜中書侍郎、同中書門下三品，賜爵臨淮男。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Yu was made heir, Yizhi took part in the plot and was promoted to vice director of the Secretariat and third-rank councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery, and was enfeoffed as Baron of Linhuai.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Yu was made heir, Yizhi took part in the plot and was promoted to vice director and third-rank councilor, enfeoffed as Baron of Linhuai.

sentences.zh: 時軍國多事，所有詔敕，獨出禕之，構思敏速，皆可立待。

translations.literal: At that time military and state affairs were many; all edicts and orders issued from Yizhi alone; his composing thought was swift, and all could be awaited standing.
translations.idiomatic: At that time military and civil affairs were heavy, and all edicts issued from Yizhi alone. His mind was quick, and every draft was ready on the spot.

sentences.zh: 及官名改易，禕之為鳳閣侍郎、同鳳閣鸞台三品。

translations.literal: When official titles were changed, Yizhi became vice director of the Phoenix Pavilion and third-rank councilor of the Phoenix Pavilion and Phoenix Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: When titles were reorganized, Yizhi became vice director of the Phoenix Pavilion and third-rank councilor.

sentences.zh: 時有司門員外郎房先敏得罪，左授衛州司馬，詣宰相陳訴。

translations.literal: At that time the vice director of the Department of Justice Fang Xianmin had offended and was demoted to steward of Wei Prefecture; he went to the chief ministers to state his grievance.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Fang Xianmin, vice director of the Department of Justice, had offended and been demoted to steward of Wei Prefecture. He went to the chief ministers to plead his case.

sentences.zh: 內史騫味道謂曰：“此乃皇太后處分也。”

translations.literal: The Director Qian Weidao said to him: "This was the Empress Dowager's disposition."
translations.idiomatic: Director Qian Weidao told him: "This was the Empress Dowager's decision."

sentences.zh: 禕之謂先敏曰：“緣坐改官，例從臣下奏請。”

translations.literal: Yizhi said to Xianmin: "When office is changed because of implicated guilt, by precedent it follows a memorial request from subordinates."
translations.idiomatic: Yizhi told Xianmin: "When someone is demoted for implicated guilt, the change is normally submitted by a minister on the emperor's behalf."

sentences.zh: 則天聞之，以味道善則歸己，過則推君，貶青州刺史。

translations.literal: When Zetian heard of it, because Weidao attributed what was good to himself and pushed what was wrong onto the ruler, she demoted him to prefect of Qing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Zetian heard this, she concluded that Weidao took credit for what was good and blamed the ruler for what was wrong, and demoted him to prefect of Qing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 以禕之推善於君，引過在己，加授太中大夫，賜物百段、細馬一匹。

translations.literal: Because Yizhi attributed what was good to the ruler and took blame upon himself, she additionally granted him Grand Master and gave him a hundred lengths of goods and one fine horse.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yizhi gave credit to the ruler and took blame upon himself, she promoted him to grand master and gave him a hundred lengths of goods and a fine horse.

sentences.zh: 因謂侍臣曰：“夫為臣之體，在揚君之德，君德發揚，豈非臣下之美事？

translations.literal: She then said to the attending ministers: "The substance of being a minister lies in exalting the ruler's virtue; when the ruler's virtue is exalted, is that not a fine thing for subordinates?
translations.idiomatic: She then told the attending ministers: "The duty of a minister is to exalt the ruler's virtue. When the ruler's virtue shines forth, is that not the minister's finest achievement?

sentences.zh: 且君為元首，臣作股肱，情同休戚，義均一體。

translations.literal: Moreover, the ruler is the head and ministers are the arms and legs; in feeling they share weal and woe, in righteousness they are one body.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler is the head and ministers are the limbs. In feeling they share weal and woe; in duty they are one body.

sentences.zh: 未聞以手足之疾移於腹背，而得一體安者。

translations.literal: One has never heard of shifting the illness of the limbs onto the belly and back and thereby obtaining the peace of one body.
translations.idiomatic: One never hears of shifting an ailment of the limbs onto the trunk and expecting the whole body to be well.

sentences.zh: 味道不存忠赤，已從屏退。

translations.literal: Weidao did not preserve loyal sincerity and has already been removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Weidao lacked loyal sincerity and has already been dismissed.

sentences.zh: 禕之竭忠奉上，情甚可嘉。”

translations.literal: Yizhi exhausts loyalty in serving above; his sentiment is greatly praiseworthy."
translations.idiomatic: Yizhi serves the throne with complete loyalty, and that is greatly to his credit."

sentences.zh: 納言王德真對曰：“昔戴至德每有善事，必推於君。”

translations.literal: Counselor Wang Dezhen replied: "In former times Dai Zhide, whenever there was a good deed, always attributed it to the ruler."
translations.idiomatic: Counselor Wang Dezhen replied: "In former times Dai Zhide always gave the ruler credit for every good deed."

sentences.zh: 太后曰：“先朝每稱至德能有此事，逮其終歿，有制褒崇。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager said: "The former court often praised Zhide for being able to do this; when he finally died, there was an edict commending and honoring him.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager said: "The former court often praised Zhide for this. When he died, an edict commended and honored him.

sentences.zh: 為臣之道，豈過斯行，傳名萬代，可不善歟！”

translations.literal: The way of being a minister—can it surpass this conduct? To transmit one's name for ten thousand generations—is that not excellent!"
translations.idiomatic: Can the way of a minister surpass such conduct? To leave one's name for ten thousand generations—what could be finer?"

sentences.zh: 儀鳳中，吐蕃為邊患，高宗謂侍臣曰：“吐蕃小丑，屢犯邊境，我比務在安輯，未即誅夷。

translations.literal: In the Yifeng era the Tibetans were a border trouble; Emperor Gaozong said to the attending ministers: "The Tibetan bandits are a petty trouble who repeatedly violate the frontier; We have lately been intent on pacification and have not yet punished them to extinction.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yifeng era Tibet was a border menace. Gaozong told his ministers: "These Tibetan raiders are a petty nuisance who keep violating the frontier. We have lately sought pacification and have not yet destroyed them.

sentences.zh: 而戎狄豺狼，不識恩造，置之則疆場日駭，圖之則未聞上策，宜論得失，各盡所懷。”

translations.literal: Yet these barbarian wolves do not recognize the grace shown them; if left alone the borderlands are daily alarmed, and if plotted against no superior strategy has been heard—each should discuss gain and loss and fully express what is in his mind."
translations.idiomatic: Yet these barbarian wolves do not recognize our kindness. If we leave them alone the border is alarmed daily; if we strike, no superior strategy has yet been found. Let each of you discuss the pros and cons and speak your mind fully."

sentences.zh: 時劉景仙、郭正一、皇甫文亮、楊思征、薛元超各有所奏。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Jingxian, Guo Zhengyi, Huangfu Wenliang, Yang Sizheng, and Xue Yuanchao each submitted their views.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jingxian, Guo Zhengyi, Huangfu Wenliang, Yang Sizheng, and Xue Yuanchao each submitted memorials.

sentences.zh: 禕之時為中書舍人，對曰：“臣觀自古明王聖主，皆患夷狄。

translations.literal: Yizhi was then drafting officer of the Secretariat and replied: "Your subject observes that from antiquity enlightened kings and sagely rulers have all been troubled by barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhi was then a drafting officer and replied: "I observe that enlightened kings and sage rulers in every age have been troubled by barbarians.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃時擾邊隅，有同禽獸，得其土地，不可攸居，被其憑淩，未足為恥。

translations.literal: The Tibetans at times harass the border regions, like birds and beasts; gaining their land cannot be dwelt in, and being relied upon and bullied by them is not enough to count as shame.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetans harass the border like wild beasts. Their land cannot be settled, and to suffer their raids is no great disgrace.

sentences.zh: 願戢萬乘之威，且寬百姓之役。”

translations.literal: Your subject wishes to restrain the majesty of the myriad chariots and for the time being ease the labor of the common people."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Your Majesty restrain the imperial majesty for now and ease the burdens on the people."

sentences.zh: 高宗嘉其言。

translations.literal: Gaozong praised his words.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong approved of his advice.

sentences.zh: 後禕之嚐竊謂鳳閣舍人賈大隱曰：“太后既能廢昏立明，何用臨朝稱制？

translations.literal: Later Yizhi once privately said to the drafting officer of the Phoenix Pavilion Jia Dayin: "Since the Empress Dowager was able to depose the dim and establish the bright, why must she hold court and assume regency?
translations.idiomatic: Later Yizhi once privately told drafting officer Jia Dayin: "Since the Empress Dowager could depose a bad ruler and set up a good one, why must she hold court and rule in regency?

sentences.zh: 不如返政，以安天下之心。”

translations.literal: It would be better to return power and thereby settle the hearts of all under Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: She would do better to return power and thereby reassure the empire."

sentences.zh: 大隱密奏其言。

translations.literal: Dayin secretly reported his words.
translations.idiomatic: Dayin reported this secretly.

sentences.zh: 則天不悅，謂左右曰：“禕之我所引用，乃有背我之心，豈復顧我恩也！”

translations.literal: Zetian was displeased and said to those around her: "Yizhi is one I myself promoted, yet he has a heart that turns against me—how can he still care for my favor!"
translations.idiomatic: Zetian was displeased and told her attendants: "Yizhi is a man I myself promoted, yet he turns against me. Does he still care for my kindness?"

sentences.zh: 垂拱三年，或誣告禕之受歸州都督孫萬榮金，兼與許敬宗妾有私，則天特令肅州刺史王本立推鞫其事。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chuigong someone falsely accused Yizhi of receiving gold from Sun Wanrong, regional commander of Guizhou, and also of having a private affair with a concubine of Xu Jingye; Zetian specially ordered Wang Benli, prefect of Su Prefecture, to investigate and examine the matter.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Chuigong someone falsely accused Yizhi of taking gold from Sun Wanrong, regional commander of Guizhou, and of having an affair with a concubine of Xu Jingye. Zetian specially ordered Su Prefecture prefect Wang Benli to investigate.

sentences.zh: 本立宣敕示禕之，禕之曰：“不經鳳閣鸞台，何名為敕？”

translations.literal: Benli proclaimed the edict and showed it to Yizhi; Yizhi said: "If it does not pass through the Phoenix Pavilion and Phoenix Terrace, what is it called an edict?"
translations.idiomatic: Benli proclaimed the edict to Yizhi. Yizhi said: "If it does not pass through the Phoenix Pavilion and Phoenix Terrace, what makes it an edict?"

sentences.zh: 則天大怒，以為拒捍製使，乃賜死於家，時年五十七。

translations.literal: Zetian was greatly angered, took it as resisting and defying the imperial commissioner, and ordered him to die by gift at home; he was then fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: Zetian was furious, took this as defiance of an imperial commissioner, and ordered him to take his own life at home. He was fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 初，禕之既下獄，睿宗為之抗疏申理，禕之親友咸以為必見原宥，竊賀之。

translations.literal: At first, after Yizhi had been imprisoned, Ruizong submitted a forthright memorial pleading his case; Yizhi's kin and friends all believed he would certainly be pardoned and secretly congratulated him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yizhi was imprisoned, Ruizong submitted a forthright memorial on his behalf. His kin and friends all believed he would be pardoned and secretly congratulated him.

sentences.zh: 禕之曰：“吾必死矣。

translations.literal: Yizhi said: "I am sure to die.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhi said: "I am sure to die.

sentences.zh: 太后臨朝獨斷，威福任己，皇帝上表，徒使速吾禍也。”

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager holds court with sole authority, wielding power as she wishes; the emperor's memorial on my behalf will only hasten my disaster."
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager rules alone, wielding power as she pleases; the emperor's memorial on my behalf will only hasten my ruin."

sentences.zh: 禕之在獄時，嚐上疏自陳。

translations.literal: While in prison, Yizhi once submitted a memorial pleading his own case.
translations.idiomatic: While in prison, Yizhi once submitted a memorial in his own defense.

sentences.zh: 及臨終，既洗沐，而神色自若，命其子執筆草謝表，其子將絕，殆不能書。

translations.literal: When the end came, after bathing, his expression remained composed; he ordered his son to take up the brush and draft a letter of thanks, but as his son was near death he could hardly write.
translations.idiomatic: At the end, after bathing, he remained composed and ordered his son to draft a letter of thanks, but his son, near death himself, could barely write.

sentences.zh: 監刑者促之。

translations.literal: The execution supervisor urged him on.
translations.idiomatic: The execution supervisor pressed him.

sentences.zh: 禕之乃自操數紙，援筆立成，詞理懇至，見者無不傷痛。

translations.literal: Yizhi then took several sheets himself, seized the brush, and at once finished the draft; the words and reasoning were earnest and moving, and none who saw it were not grieved.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhi then took several sheets himself, seized the brush, and finished at once. The words were earnest and moving, and all who saw them were grieved.

sentences.zh: 時麟台郎郭翰、太子文學周思鈞共稱歎其文，則天聞而惡之，左遷翰為巫州司法，思鈞為播州司倉。

translations.literal: At the time Linnetai Officer Guo Han and Crown Prince Literary Scholar Zhou Sijun together praised his writing; Zetian heard of this and was angered, demoting Han to judicial officer of Wu Prefecture and Sijun to granary officer of Bo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Linnetai officer Guo Han and crown prince literary scholar Zhou Sijun praised his writing. Zetian heard of this and was angered, demoting Han to judicial officer of Wu Prefecture and Sijun to granary officer of Bo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 睿宗即位，以禕之宮府舊僚，追贈中書令。

translations.literal: When Ruizong took the throne, because Yizhi had been an old colleague in his princely household, he was posthumously granted Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruizong took the throne, he posthumously made Yizhi Director of the Secretariat as an old colleague from his princely household.

sentences.zh: 有集七十卷，傳於時。

translations.literal: He left a collected works in seventy scrolls, which circulated in his time.
translations.idiomatic: He left collected works in seventy scrolls that circulated in his day.

sentences.zh: 魏玄同，定州鼓城人也。

translations.literal: Wei Xuantong was a man of Gucheng in Ding Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xuantong was a native of Gucheng in Ding Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 舉進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 累轉司列大夫。

translations.literal: He was successively transferred to the post of Grand Master of the Bureau of Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to become Grand Master of the Bureau of Appointments.

sentences.zh: 坐與上官儀文章屬和，配流嶺外。

translations.literal: Because he collaborated with Shangguan Yi in composing literary works, he was sentenced to exile beyond the Ling mountains.
translations.idiomatic: He was exiled beyond the Ling region for collaborating with Shangguan Yi on literary compositions.

sentences.zh: 上元初赦還。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Shangyuan era he was pardoned and returned.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Shangyuan reign he was pardoned and allowed to return.

sentences.zh: 工部尚書劉審禮薦玄同有時務之才，拜岐州長史。

translations.literal: Liu Shenli, Minister of Works, recommended Xuantong as possessed of talent for current affairs, and he was appointed Long History of Qi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Liu Shenli recommended Xuantong for his grasp of practical affairs, and he was appointed chief secretary of Qi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 累遷至吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was successively promoted to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to become vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 玄同以既委選舉，恐未盡得人之術，乃上疏曰：

translations.literal: Xuantong, having been entrusted with selection and appointment, feared that the methods for obtaining the right men had not been fully applied, and so submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Now charged with civil appointments, Xuantong feared the system still failed to secure the right men, and submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 臣聞製器者必擇匠以簡材，為國者必求賢以蒞官。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that one who makes vessels must choose craftsmen to select materials, and one who governs a state must seek the worthy to take up office.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that those who fashion vessels must choose skilled craftsmen to pick their materials, and those who govern a state must seek worthy men to fill its offices.

sentences.zh: 匠之不良，無以成其工；

translations.literal: If the craftsman is inferior, there is no way to complete the work;
translations.idiomatic: Without a capable craftsman, the work cannot be done well;

sentences.zh: 官之非賢，無以致於理。

translations.literal: if the official is not worthy, there is no way to achieve good order.
translations.idiomatic: without worthy officials, good government is impossible.

sentences.zh: 君者，所以牧人也；

translations.literal: The ruler is one who tends the people;
translations.idiomatic: The ruler exists to shepherd the people;

sentences.zh: 臣者，所以佐君也。

translations.literal: ministers are those who assist the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: ministers exist to assist the ruler.

sentences.zh: 君不養人，失君道矣；

translations.literal: If the ruler does not nurture the people, he fails the way of rulership;
translations.idiomatic: When a ruler fails to nurture the people, he abandons the duty of kingship;

sentences.zh: 臣不輔君，失臣任矣。

translations.literal: if ministers do not assist the ruler, they fail the charge of ministerial service.
translations.idiomatic: when ministers fail to assist the ruler, they neglect their office.

sentences.zh: 任人者，誠國家之基本，百姓之安危也。

translations.literal: The appointment of men is truly the foundation of the state and the security or peril of the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Appointing the right men is truly the foundation of the state and the key to the people's welfare or ruin.

sentences.zh: 方今人不加富，盜賊不衰，獄公未清，禮義猶闕者，何也？

translations.literal: At present the people are not growing richer, bandits and thieves are not diminishing, public prisons are not cleared, and ritual and righteousness are still lacking—why is this?
translations.idiomatic: Why is it that today the people grow no richer, crime does not abate, the courts remain clogged, and ritual and righteousness are still wanting?

sentences.zh: 下吏不稱職，庶官非其才也。

translations.literal: Lower officials do not fulfill their duties, and the multitude of offices are not filled by men of suitable talent.
translations.idiomatic: The reason is that lower officials do not perform their duties and many posts are held by men unfit for them.

sentences.zh: 官之不得其才者，取人之道，有所未盡也。

translations.literal: When offices do not obtain suitable talent, it is because the way of selecting men has not been fully carried out.
translations.idiomatic: When offices lack fit men, the methods of selection have not been fully applied.

sentences.zh: 臣又聞傳說曰：“明王奉若天道，建邦設都，樹後王君公，承以大夫師長，不惟逸豫，惟以理人。”

translations.literal: Your subject has also heard that Fu Yue said: "The enlightened king follows Heaven's Way, establishes states and sets up capitals, installs heirs, kings, lords, and dukes, and supports them with grandees, masters, and elders—not seeking ease and pleasure alone, but only to govern the people."
translations.idiomatic: I have also heard Fu Yue say: "The enlightened king follows Heaven's Way, founds states and establishes capitals, appoints heirs, kings, lords, and dukes, and supports them with ministers and mentors—not for ease and pleasure, but to govern the people."

sentences.zh: 昔之邦國，今之州縣，士有常君，人有定主，自求臣佐，各選英賢，其大臣乃命於王朝耳。

translations.literal: The states of old are the prefectures and counties of today; scholars had fixed lords, and men had settled masters; each sought his own assistants and chosen worthies, and only the great ministers were appointed by the royal court.
translations.idiomatic: The feudal states of antiquity are today's prefectures and counties. Men of talent served fixed lords; each lord found his own aides and chose his own worthies. Only the highest ministers received appointment from the throne.

sentences.zh: 秦併天下，罷侯置守，漢氏因之，有沿有革。

translations.literal: When Qin united the realm, it abolished feudal lords and set up commandants; the Han followed this, with some continuity and some change.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin united the empire it abolished the feudal lords and appointed commandants in their place. Han inherited that system, retaining some parts and changing others.

sentences.zh: 諸侯得自置吏四百石以下，其傅相大官，則漢為置之。

translations.literal: Feudal lords could appoint officials of four hundred shi rank and below on their own; as for tutors, chancellors, and great offices, Han appointed them.
translations.idiomatic: Feudal lords could appoint their own officials below the rank of four hundred shi, but tutors, chancellors, and high posts were appointed by the Han court.

sentences.zh: 州郡掾吏、督郵從事，悉任之於牧守。

translations.literal: Prefectural and commandery clerks, supervisors, and attendants were all entrusted to the governors and commandants.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural and commandery staff, inspectors, and attendants were all left to the discretion of regional governors.

sentences.zh: 爰自魏、晉，始歸吏部，遞相祖襲，以迄於今。

translations.literal: From Wei and Jin onward, this power returned to the Ministry of Personnel; one dynasty after another inherited the practice down to the present day.
translations.idiomatic: From Wei and Jin onward, appointment authority passed to the Ministry of Personnel, and dynasty after dynasty preserved the practice down to our own day.

sentences.zh: 用刀筆以量才，案簿書而察行，法令之弊，其來自久。

translations.literal: Using brush and knife to measure talent and checking records and documents to inspect conduct—the flaws of this legalistic method have long existed.
translations.idiomatic: Talent is measured by paperwork and conduct judged from ledgers—this bureaucratic method has been flawed for a very long time.

sentences.zh: 蓋君子重因循而憚改作，有不得已者，亦當運獨見之明，定卓然之議。

translations.literal: Generally gentlemen value continuity and fear innovation; when there is no choice, one should nevertheless apply exceptional insight and settle on a decisive policy.
translations.idiomatic: Men of principle cherish continuity and shrink from reform, but when necessity demands it, one should apply independent judgment and settle on a bold policy.

sentences.zh: 如今選司所行者，非上皇之令典，乃近代之權道，所宜遷徙，實為至要。

translations.literal: What the selection bureau now practices is not the fixed ordinances of the High Emperor but a provisional expedient of recent times; it ought to be changed, and this is truly of utmost importance.
translations.idiomatic: What the selection bureau now follows is not the permanent law of the founding emperor but a temporary expedient of recent centuries. Reform is urgently needed.

sentences.zh: 何以言之？

translations.literal: How may this be explained?
translations.idiomatic: Why do I say so?

sentences.zh: 夫尺丈之量，所及者蓋短；

translations.literal: As for the measure of feet and spans, what it can reach is generally short;
translations.idiomatic: A ruler of feet and spans can measure only so far;

sentences.zh: 鍾庾之器，所積者寧多。

translations.literal: as for vessels of grain measures, what they can hold is surely much.
translations.idiomatic: a granary vessel can hold far more.

sentences.zh: 非其所及，焉能度之；

translations.literal: What lies beyond their reach—how can they measure it?
translations.idiomatic: What lies beyond their reach cannot be measured by them;

sentences.zh: 非其所受，何以容之？

translations.literal: What they cannot contain—how can they hold it?
translations.idiomatic: what they cannot hold cannot be stored in them.

sentences.zh: 況天下之大，士人之眾，而可委之數人之手乎？

translations.literal: Moreover, with the vastness of the realm and the multitude of scholars, how can this be entrusted to the hands of a few men?
translations.idiomatic: How, then, can the vast empire and its countless men of talent be entrusted to a handful of officials?

sentences.zh: 假使平如權衡，明如水鏡，力有所極，照有所窮，銓綜既多，紊失斯廣。

translations.literal: Even supposing they were as level as scales and as bright as a water mirror, strength has its limits and illumination its bounds; with so many to evaluate and rank, disorder and error become all the wider.
translations.idiomatic: Even if they were as even as scales and as clear as mirrors, their strength would have limits and their vision bounds. With so many candidates to assess, confusion and error would multiply.

sentences.zh: 又以比居此任，時有非人。

translations.literal: Moreover, those who successively hold this post are at times unworthy men.
translations.idiomatic: Worse, those who hold this office are not always fit for it.

sentences.zh: 豈直愧彼清通，昧於甄察；

translations.literal: How could they merely shame those who are pure and penetrating through blindness in discrimination?
translations.idiomatic: It is not only that the unworthy disgrace the discerning and fail at selection;

sentences.zh: 亦將竟其庸妄，糅彼棼絲。

translations.literal: They will also carry their mediocrity and presumption to the end and tangle affairs like snarled silk.
translations.idiomatic: they also indulge their mediocrity to the full and tangle affairs like knotted silk.

sentences.zh: 情故既行，何所不至？

translations.literal: Once favoritism is practiced, what will not follow?
translations.idiomatic: Once favoritism begins, what limit can there be?

sentences.zh: 髒私一啟，以及萬端。

translations.literal: Once corrupt private dealings are opened, they extend to countless other abuses.
translations.idiomatic: Once corrupt private dealings are allowed, a thousand other abuses follow.

sentences.zh: 至乃為人擇官，為身擇利，顧親疏而下筆，看勢要而措情。

translations.literal: It even reaches the point of choosing offices for men and profit for oneself, taking account of kinship in wielding the brush and adjusting sentiment according to the powerful.
translations.idiomatic: Officials even choose posts for particular men and profits for themselves, letting kinship guide their pen and influence their judgment according to the powerful.

sentences.zh: 悠悠風塵，此焉奔兢；

translations.literal: In the endless dust of the world, here men rush in rivalry;
translations.idiomatic: In the restless world of official life, men scramble here for advantage;

sentences.zh: 擾擾遊宦，同乎市井。

translations.literal: the tumult of office-seeking is no different from the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: the turmoil of official ambition becomes indistinguishable from haggling in the market.

sentences.zh: 加以厚貌深衷，險如溪壑，擇言觀行，猶懼不周。

translations.literal: To this add faces thick and hearts deep, treacherous as ravines and gullies—in choosing words and observing conduct, one still fears incompleteness.
translations.idiomatic: Add to this that men wear thick masks and hide deep designs, treacherous as ravines—careful scrutiny of words and conduct still falls short.

sentences.zh: 今使百行九能，折之於一面，具僚庶品，專斷於一司，不亦難矣！

translations.literal: Now to make a hundred virtues and nine talents be judged on one side alone, and all officials of every rank be decided by one bureau—is this not difficult!
translations.idiomatic: To judge a man's full character from a single impression and let one bureau decide the fate of every official—is this not impossible!

sentences.zh: 且魏人應運，所據者乃三分；

translations.literal: Moreover, when Wei rose in response to Heaven's mandate, what it held was only one of three parts;
translations.idiomatic: When Wei rose to power, it ruled only a third of the realm;

sentences.zh: 晉氏播遷，所臨者非一統。

translations.literal: when Jin was driven into exile, what it ruled was not a unified realm.
translations.idiomatic: when Jin fled south, it did not govern a unified empire.

sentences.zh: 逮乎齊、宋，以及周、隋，戰爭之日多，安泰之時少，瓜分瓦裂，各在一方。

translations.literal: Down through Qi and Song, and on to Zhou and Sui, days of war were many and days of peace few; the realm was carved and shattered, each part in its own corner.
translations.idiomatic: From Qi and Song through Zhou and Sui, war outlasted peace and the realm lay divided, each dynasty holding its own fragment.

sentences.zh: 隋氏平陳，十餘年耳，接以兵禍，繼以饑饉，既德業之不逮，或時事所未遑，非謂是今而非古也。

translations.literal: When Sui conquered Chen, it was only a little more than ten years before war's disasters followed and famine succeeded; whether because virtue and achievement fell short or because the times left no leisure, this is not to say that the present is right and antiquity wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Sui conquered Chen and ruled for little more than a decade before war and famine struck. Whether because virtue was lacking or because events allowed no other course, this is not to praise the present and condemn antiquity.

sentences.zh: 武德、貞觀，與今亦異，皇運之初，庶事草創，豈唯日不暇給，亦乃人物常稀。

translations.literal: The Wude and Zhenguan eras differed from today as well; at the beginning of the imperial destiny, all affairs were newly established—not only were the days not enough, but men of talent were also commonly scarce.
translations.idiomatic: The Wude and Zhenguan periods differed from our own as well. At the dynasty's founding everything was being built from scratch; not only was there no time to spare, but worthy men were scarce.

sentences.zh: 天祚大聖，享國永年，比屋可封，異人間出。

translations.literal: Heaven has granted great sagacity and long enjoyment of the realm; every household may be worthy of enfeoffment, and extraordinary men appear one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven has endowed us with sage rule and long years of peace; every household seems worthy of honor, and extraordinary talent appears at every turn.

sentences.zh: 咸以為有道恥賤，得時無怠，諸色入流，歲以千計。

translations.literal: All alike, holding that under the Way it is shameful to remain in low station and that one should not be idle when the time is right, enter the official stream in every category, numbering thousands each year.
translations.idiomatic: Believing it shameful to remain obscure under enlightened rule and eager to seize the moment, candidates in every category enter the official ranks by the thousand each year.

sentences.zh: 群司列位，無復新加，官有常員，人無定限。

translations.literal: Offices throughout the administration no longer receive new additions, posts have fixed quotas, but men have no fixed limit.
translations.idiomatic: The bureaucracy no longer expands its posts; offices have fixed quotas, but candidates have none.

sentences.zh: 選集之始，霧積雲屯，擢敘於終，十不收一。

translations.literal: At the beginning of selection gatherings they pile up like mist and cloud; at the end when promotions are made, not one in ten is chosen.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of each selection season candidates swarm like clouds; by the end, fewer than one in ten wins appointment.

sentences.zh: 淄澠雜混，玉石難分，用舍去留，得失相半。

translations.literal: The Zi and the Sheng are mingled and jade and stone are hard to distinguish; in employing or rejecting, keeping or dismissing, gain and loss are half and half.
translations.idiomatic: Good and bad are hopelessly mixed, jade indistinguishable from stone; who is kept and who is dismissed seems a matter of pure chance.

sentences.zh: 撫即事之為弊，知及後之滋失。

translations.literal: Touch the present affair and see its harm; understand it and foresee the growing loss hereafter.
translations.idiomatic: Consider the harm of the present system and one can foresee how much worse it will become.

sentences.zh: 夏、殷已前，制度多闕，周監二代，煥乎可睹。

translations.literal: Before Xia and Yin, institutions were largely lacking; Zhou took warning from the two dynasties, and its brilliance is plain to see.
translations.idiomatic: Before Xia and Shang, institutions were largely incomplete. Zhou learned from the two earlier dynasties, and its model shines clearly before us.

sentences.zh: 豈諸侯之臣，不皆命於天子，王朝庶官，亦不專於一職。

translations.literal: Were not all the ministers of the feudal lords appointed by the Son of Heaven? The multitude of offices of the royal court were not monopolized by one position alone.
translations.idiomatic: Surely not every minister of the feudal lords was appointed by the Son of Heaven—and the court's many offices were not monopolized by a single bureau.

sentences.zh: 故周穆王以伯冏為太僕正，命之曰：“慎簡乃僚，無以巧言令色便僻側媚，唯吉士。”

translations.literal: Therefore King Mu of Zhou appointed Bo Jiong as Director of the Imperial Stud and commanded him, saying: "Carefully select your subordinates; do not employ smooth words, pleasing countenance, cleverness, perversity, or fawning flattery—only good men."
translations.idiomatic: King Mu of Zhou appointed Bo Jiong Director of the Imperial Stud and told him: "Choose your subordinates with care. Do not take men of smooth speech, pleasing faces, cunning tricks, perversity, or obsequious flattery—only good men."

sentences.zh: 此則令其自擇下吏之文也。

translations.literal: This is the language by which he was ordered to choose his own lower officials.
translations.idiomatic: This is the charge to choose one's own subordinates.

sentences.zh: 太僕正，中大夫耳，尚以僚屬委之，則三公九卿，亦必然矣。

translations.literal: The Director of the Imperial Stud was only a middle grandee, yet even the appointment of subordinates was entrusted to him; the Three Dukes and Nine Ministers would necessarily be the same.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of the Imperial Stud was only a middle-ranking minister, yet even his staff were left to his choice—how much more so for the Three Dukes and Nine Ministers.

sentences.zh: 《周禮》：太宰、內史，並掌爵祿廢置；

translations.literal: The Rites of Zhou states: the Grand Steward and the Inner Scribe both administer enfeoffment, salary, dismissal, and appointment;
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou assigns enfeoffment, salary, dismissal, and appointment jointly to the Grand Steward and the Inner Scribe;

sentences.zh: 司徒、司馬，別掌興賢詔事。

translations.literal: the Minister of Education and the Minister of War separately administer the promotion of worthies and proclamation of affairs.
translations.idiomatic: while the Minister of Education and the Minister of War separately oversee the raising up of worthies and public appointments.

sentences.zh: 當是分任於群司，而統之以數職，各自求其小者，而王命其大者焉。

translations.literal: This should mean dividing responsibility among the various bureaus while coordinating them through several offices—each seeking the lesser men on his own, while the king appoints the greater men.
translations.idiomatic: Responsibility was divided among many offices and coordinated through several posts: each minister found his own junior staff, while the king appointed the senior men.

sentences.zh: 夫委任責成，君之體也，所委者當，所用者精，故能得濟濟之多士，盛芃芃之棫樸。

translations.literal: Entrusting duty and demanding results is the substance of rulership; when those entrusted are appropriate and those employed are chosen with care, one can thereby obtain the many scholars in abundance and the flourishing host of uncarved timber.
translations.idiomatic: To delegate responsibility and demand results is the essence of kingship. When the right men are entrusted and the right talents employed, the state gains a host of able scholars and a rich store of uncarved timber.

sentences.zh: 裴子野有言曰：“官人之難，先王言之尚矣。

translations.literal: Pei Ziye once said: "The difficulty of appointing officials—the former kings spoke of it long ago.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ziye wrote: "The difficulty of appointing officials—the ancient kings spoke of it long ago.

sentences.zh: 居家視其孝友，鄉黨服其誠信，出入觀其誌義，憂歡取其智謀。

translations.literal: Observe filial piety and brotherliness at home, observe trustworthiness and sincerity in the village community, observe loyalty and righteousness in going out and coming in, and in sorrow and joy take note of wisdom and planning.
translations.idiomatic: Watch a man's filial piety and brotherliness at home, his honesty in the community, his loyalty in public life, and his wisdom in times of trouble or joy.

sentences.zh: 煩之以事，以觀其能；

translations.literal: Trouble him with affairs to observe his ability;
translations.idiomatic: Burden him with work to test his ability;

sentences.zh: 臨之以利，以察其廉。

translations.literal: confront him with profit to examine his integrity.
translations.idiomatic: tempt him with gain to test his integrity.

sentences.zh: 《周禮》始於學校，論之州里，告諸六事，而後貢之王庭。

translations.literal: The Rites of Zhou begin with the schools, discuss men in the district and village, report the six affairs, and only then present them to the royal court.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou begins in the schools, evaluates men in their districts, reports on the six virtues, and only then sends them to the royal court.

sentences.zh: 其在漢家，尚猶然矣。

translations.literal: In the Han house as well, it was still thus.
translations.idiomatic: Han followed much the same course.

sentences.zh: 州郡積其功能，然後為五府所辟，五府舉其掾屬而升於朝，三公參得除署，尚書奏之天子。

translations.literal: Prefectures and commanderies accumulated records of merit and ability; only then were men summoned by the five offices; the five offices promoted their clerks and attendants to the court; the Three Dukes jointly obtained the power of appointment; and the Imperial Secretariat reported to the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures and commanderies first tracked men's service; then the five ministries recruited them, promoting their staff to court; the Three Dukes shared appointment authority; and the Secretariat presented the list to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 一人之身，所關者眾；

translations.literal: A single man's person involves many who are concerned;
translations.idiomatic: Many eyes weighed a single candidate;

sentences.zh: 一士之進，其謀也詳。

translations.literal: a single scholar's advancement was deliberated with care.
translations.idiomatic: and his promotion was carefully considered.

sentences.zh: 故官得其人，鮮有敗事。

translations.literal: Therefore when offices obtained the right men, failure in affairs was rare.
translations.idiomatic: When offices had the right men, failure was rare.

sentences.zh: 魏、晉反是，所失弘多。”

translations.literal: Wei and Jin reversed this, and their losses were very great."
translations.idiomatic: Wei and Jin reversed this practice, and the cost was enormous."

sentences.zh: 子野所論，蓋區區之宋朝耳，猶謂不勝其弊，而況於當今乎！

translations.literal: What Ziye discussed concerned merely the petty Song dynasty, yet he still judged its defects beyond remedy—how much more so in the present day!
translations.idiomatic: Ziye was writing about the small Song state alone, yet even that system he found beyond repair—how much more so today!

sentences.zh: 又夫從政蒞官，不可以無學。

translations.literal: Moreover, in taking part in government and holding office, one cannot do without learning.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, no one can hold office and govern without education.

sentences.zh: 故《書》曰：“學古入官，議事以制。”

translations.literal: Therefore the Book of Documents says: "Study antiquity to enter office; deliberate on affairs according to established norms."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Documents says: "Study the ancients before taking office; discuss affairs according to established norms."

sentences.zh: 《傳》曰：“我聞學以從政，不聞以政入學。”

translations.literal: The Commentary says: "I have heard of learning in order to enter government, not of entering government in order to learn."
translations.idiomatic: The Commentary says: "I have heard of learning in order to govern, not of governing in order to learn."

sentences.zh: 今貴戚子弟，例早求官，髫齔之年，已腰銀艾，或童草之歲，已襲朱紫。

translations.literal: Today the sons and younger brothers of the nobility, as a rule, seek office early; in the years when hair is still down on the temples they already wear silver seals and green sashes, or in the years of tender shoots they already inherit crimson and purple.
translations.idiomatic: Today noble sons routinely seek office while still young. While their hair is still on their temples they already wear silver seals; while still mere boys they already inherit purple robes.

sentences.zh: 弘文崇賢之生，千牛輦腳之類，課試既淺，藝能亦薄，而門閥有素，資望自高。

translations.literal: Students of the Hongwen and Chongxian academies and men of categories such as Thousand-Ox Attendants and carriage runners—their examination standards are shallow and their arts and abilities meager, yet their great families have long standing and their qualifications and standing are naturally high.
translations.idiomatic: Students of the Hongwen and Chongxian academies and men from posts such as Thousand-Ox Attendant face shallow examinations and show thin ability, yet their great-house pedigree lifts their standing.

sentences.zh: 夫象賢繼父，古之道也。

translations.literal: To model worthiness and succeed one's father is the Way of antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: To emulate a worthy father and succeed him is the ancient way.

sentences.zh: 所謂胄子，必裁諸學，修六禮以節其性，明七教以興其德，齊八政以防其淫，舉上賢以崇德，簡不肖以黜惡。

translations.literal: What are called scions of noble families must be shaped in the schools: cultivate the six rites to regulate their nature, clarify the seven teachings to raise their virtue, align the eight policies to guard against excess, promote the superior and worthy to honor virtue, and select out the unworthy to dismiss the wicked.
translations.idiomatic: Noble heirs were to be trained in school: taught the six rites to discipline their nature, the seven virtues to cultivate their character, and the eight policies to restrain excess; the worthy were to be advanced and the unworthy removed.

sentences.zh: 少則受業，長而出仕，並由德進，必以才升，然後可以利用賓王，移家事國。

translations.literal: In youth they received instruction; when grown they entered service—all advancement by virtue, promotion necessarily by talent—and only then could they serve as guests and aids to the king and transfer family affairs to the state.
translations.idiomatic: They studied in youth and entered service in maturity, advancing by virtue and rising by talent—only then could they serve the throne and turn private duty into public service.

sentences.zh: 少仕則廢學，輕試則無才，於此一流，良足惜也。

translations.literal: To enter office young is to abandon learning; to be lightly tested is to lack talent—in this one category there is truly much to regret.
translations.idiomatic: Early office means abandoned learning; easy promotion means empty talent. In this path lies real waste.

sentences.zh: 又勳官三衛流外之徒，不待州縣之舉，直取之於書判，恐非先德而後言才之義也。

translations.literal: Moreover, men of meritorious rank, the Three Guards, and those outside the regular stream, without waiting for recommendation from prefectures and counties, are taken directly through examination of documents and judgments—I fear this is not the principle of putting virtue first and talent second.
translations.idiomatic: Merit officers, Guardsmen, and men from irregular categories enter through document examinations without local recommendation—this reverses the principle of virtue before talent.

sentences.zh: 臣又以為國之用人，有似人之用財。

translations.literal: Your subject further holds that a state's use of men is like a man's use of wealth.
translations.idiomatic: I would also compare a state's use of men to a man's use of money.

sentences.zh: 貧者厭糟糠，思短褐；

translations.literal: The poor loathe chaff and husks and long for coarse cloth;
translations.idiomatic: The poor tire of chaff and crave plain cloth;

sentences.zh: 富者餘糧肉，衣輕裘。

translations.literal: the rich have surplus grain and meat and wear light furs.
translations.idiomatic: the rich have grain and meat to spare and wear fine furs.

sentences.zh: 然則當衰弊乏賢之時，則可磨策朽鈍而乘馭之；

translations.literal: Then, in times of decline, exhaustion, and lack of worthies, one may polish and spur the worn and dull and put them to use;
translations.idiomatic: In times of decline, when talent is scarce, one may sharpen worn tools and put dull horses to work;

sentences.zh: 在太平多士之日，亦宜妙選髦俊而任使之。

translations.literal: in days of great peace and abundant scholars, one should also finely select outstanding talents and employ them.
translations.idiomatic: in times of peace and abundance, one should carefully choose the finest talent available.

sentences.zh: 《詩》云：“翹翹錯薪，言刈其楚。”

translations.literal: The Book of Poetry says: "The piled firewood stands tall; they say, cut the thorn-bush."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Poetry says: "The firewood stacks high; cut the tallest thorn."

sentences.zh: 楚，荊也，在薪之翹翹者。

translations.literal: Chu is the thorn-bush—the tallest among the firewood.
translations.idiomatic: Chu is thorn—the tallest stalk in the stack.

sentences.zh: 方之用才，理亦當爾，選人幸多，尤宜簡練。

translations.literal: In employing talent it is right that the principle should be the same; with candidates fortunately abundant, selection should especially be refined.
translations.idiomatic: The same principle applies to talent: with candidates in such abundance, selection must be all the more careful.

sentences.zh: 臣竊見制書，每令三品、五品薦士，下至九品，亦令舉人，此聖朝側席旁求之意也。

translations.literal: Your subject has privately seen imperial edicts repeatedly ordering third- and fifth-rank officials to recommend scholars, and even down to ninth rank ordering the recommendation of men—this is the holy court's intent to sit aside one's seat and seek widely.
translations.idiomatic: I note that imperial edicts repeatedly order third- and fifth-rank officials to recommend talent, and even ninth-rank officials to do the same—this reflects the court's eager search for able men.

sentences.zh: 但以褒貶不甚明，得失無大隔，故人上不憂黜責，下不盡搜揚，苟以應命，莫慎所舉。

translations.literal: But because rewards and punishments are not very clear and gain and loss are not greatly separated, those above do not fear demotion and censure, and those below do not fully search and promote; if they merely respond to the order, none are careful in whom they recommend.
translations.idiomatic: But because rewards and penalties are unclear and stakes are low, superiors need not fear punishment and subordinates need not search hard; men comply with the order without caring whom they recommend.

sentences.zh: 且惟賢知賢，聖人篤論，伊、皋既舉，不仁咸遠。

translations.literal: Moreover, only the worthy know the worthy—the sages spoke emphatically of this; once Yi Yin and Gao Yao were raised up, the unworthy all kept their distance.
translations.idiomatic: Only the worthy can recognize worth—the sages said it plainly. Once Yi Yin and Gao Yao were elevated, the unworthy fell away.

sentences.zh: 復患階秩雖同，人才異等，身且濫進，鑒豈知人？

translations.literal: There is also the worry that though rank is the same, men's talents differ in grade; if one has himself advanced recklessly, how can his judgment know other men?
translations.idiomatic: There is also the problem that though ranks may match, talents do not; how can a man who bought his own way in judge others?

sentences.zh: 今欲務得實才，兼宜擇其舉主。

translations.literal: If one now wishes to strive to obtain real talent, one should also choose carefully those who make recommendations.
translations.idiomatic: To obtain genuine talent, we must also hold recommenders accountable.

sentences.zh: 流清以源潔，影端由表正，不詳舉主之行能，而責舉人之庸濫，不可得已。

translations.literal: Clear flow comes from a pure source; an upright shadow comes from a straight edge. Without examining the conduct and ability of those who make recommendations, yet blaming recommenders for careless selection—that cannot be achieved.
translations.idiomatic: Streams run clear only from a pure source; shadows fall straight only from a true edge. You cannot fault recommenders for poor choices without first judging the men who recommend.

sentences.zh: 《漢書》云：“張耳、陳餘之賓客、廝役，皆天下俊傑。”

translations.literal: The Book of Han says: "The guests and servants of Zhang Er and Chen Yu were all outstanding men under Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Han says: "The guests and servants of Zhang Er and Chen Yu were all outstanding men under Heaven."
