sentences.zh: 彼之蕞爾，猶能若斯，況以神皇之聖明，國家之德業，而不建久長之策，為無窮之基，盡得賢取士之術，而但顧望魏、晉之遺風，留意周、隋之末事，臣竊惑之。

translations.literal: Those petty men could still do thus; how much more so, with the Divine Sovereign's sagely clarity and the state's virtue and achievement, not to establish a long-lasting policy, lay a foundation without end, and fully master the art of selecting worthy men—but only look back to the leftover customs of Wei and Jin and fix attention on the last affairs of Zhou and Sui—I am privately puzzled.
translations.idiomatic: Even such petty men achieved this much; how much more should Your Majesty, with imperial wisdom and national virtue, establish enduring policy, lay a lasting foundation, and master the art of recruiting talent—rather than looking back to Wei and Jin habits and brooding over the late troubles of Zhou and Sui? I confess I am baffled.

sentences.zh: 伏願稍回聖慮，時采芻言，略依周、漢之規，以分吏部之選。

translations.literal: I humbly wish that Your Sacred consideration might turn slightly, occasionally gathering humble words, roughly following the regulations of Zhou and Han, to divide the selections of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly ask that Your Majesty turn your attention slightly, heed humble counsel from time to time, and roughly follow the Zhou and Han model by dividing the Ministry of Personnel's selections.

sentences.zh: 即望所用精詳，鮮于差失。

translations.literal: Then I hope those employed will be carefully chosen, with few errors.
translations.idiomatic: Then appointments may be made with care, and mistakes kept rare.

sentences.zh: 疏奏不納。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted but not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted but not accepted.

sentences.zh: 弘道初，轉文昌左丞，兼地官尚書、同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Hongdao, he was transferred to Left Vice Director of the Wenchang Department, concurrently Minister of the Ministry of Revenue and Third Rank at the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Hongdao, he was transferred to Left Vice Director of the Wenchang Department, concurrently Minister of the Ministry of Revenue and Third Rank at the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 則天臨朝，遷太中大夫、鸞台侍郎，依前知政事。

translations.literal: When Empress Wu assumed the throne, he was promoted to Grand Master of Palace Attendance and Vice Director of the Luantai Department, continuing as before to manage state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu assumed the throne, he was promoted to Grand Master of Palace Attendance and Vice Director of the Luantai Department, continuing as before to manage state affairs.

sentences.zh: 垂拱三年，加銀青光祿大夫，檢校納言，封钜鹿男。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chuigong, he was given the additional title Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Silver Seal, Acting Censor-in-Chief, and ennobled as Baron of Julu.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Chuigong, he was given the additional title Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Silver Seal, Acting Censor-in-Chief, and ennobled as Baron of Julu.

sentences.zh: 玄同素與裴炎結交，能保始終，時人呼為“耐久朋”。

translations.literal: Xuantong had long been friends with Pei Yan and kept their friendship to the end; people of the time called them "enduring friends."
translations.idiomatic: Xuantong had long been friends with Pei Yan and kept their friendship to the end; people of the time called them "enduring friends."

sentences.zh: 而與酷吏周興不協。

translations.literal: But he did not get along with the harsh official Zhou Xing.
translations.idiomatic: But he did not get along with the harsh official Zhou Xing.

sentences.zh: 永昌初，為周興所構，云玄同言：“太后老矣，須復皇嗣。”

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongchang, he was framed by Zhou Xing, who reported that Xuantong had said: "The Empress Dowager is old; the imperial heir must be restored."
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yongchang, he was framed by Zhou Xing, who reported that Xuantong had said: "The Empress Dowager is old; the imperial heir must be restored."

sentences.zh: 太后聞之，怒，乃賜死於家。

translations.literal: When the Empress Dowager heard this, she was enraged and ordered him granted death at home.
translations.idiomatic: When the Empress Dowager heard this, she was enraged and ordered him granted death at home.

sentences.zh: 監察御史房濟謂玄同曰：“何不告事，冀得召見，當自陳訴。”

translations.literal: Supervising Censor Fang Ji said to Xuantong: "Why not inform on others, hoping to be summoned for an audience, so you may plead your own case?"
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Censor Fang Ji said to Xuantong: "Why not inform on others, hoping to be summoned for an audience, so you may plead your own case?"

sentences.zh: 玄同歎曰：“人殺鬼殺，有何殊也，豈能為告人事乎！”

translations.literal: Xuantong sighed and said: "To be killed by men or killed by ghosts—what difference is there? How could I become an informer!"
translations.idiomatic: Xuantong sighed: "Whether men kill me or ghosts kill me, what difference does it make? I could never become an informer!"

sentences.zh: 乃就刑，年七十三。

translations.literal: He then went to execution. He was seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: He then went to execution. He was seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 子恬，開元中為潁王傅。

translations.literal: His son Tian, during the Kaiyuan era, served as tutor to the Prince of Ying.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tian, during the Kaiyuan era, served as tutor to the Prince of Ying.

sentences.zh: 李昭德

translations.literal: Li Zhaode
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhaode

sentences.zh: 李昭德，京兆長安人也。

translations.literal: Li Zhaode was a native of Chang'an in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhaode was a native of Chang'an in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 父乾祐，貞觀初為殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: His father Qianyou, in the early Zhenguan era, served as palace censor.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qianyou, in the early Zhenguan era, served as palace censor.

sentences.zh: 時有鄃令裴仁軌私役門夫，太宗欲斬之。

translations.literal: At the time the magistrate of Fu, Pei Rengui, privately conscripted gate guards for labor, and Emperor Taizong wished to behead him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the magistrate of Fu, Pei Rengui, privately conscripted gate guards for labor, and Emperor Taizong wished to behead him.

sentences.zh: 乾祐奏曰：“法令者，陛下制之於上，率土尊之於下，與天下共之，非陛下獨有也。

translations.literal: Qianyou memorialized: "The laws and ordinances are made by Your Majesty above and honored throughout the realm below—they are shared with all under Heaven, not the sole possession of Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Qianyou memorialized: "The laws and ordinances are made by Your Majesty above and honored throughout the realm below—they are shared with all under Heaven, not the sole possession of Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 仁軌犯輕罪而致極刑，是乖畫一之理。

translations.literal: Rengui committed a light offense yet would receive extreme punishment—this violates the principle of uniform application.
translations.idiomatic: Rengui committed a light offense yet would receive extreme punishment—this violates the principle of uniform application.

sentences.zh: 刑罰不中，則人無所措手足。

translations.literal: When punishments are not appropriate, people have nowhere to put hand or foot.
translations.idiomatic: When punishments are not appropriate, people have nowhere to put hand or foot.

sentences.zh: 臣忝憲司，不敢奉制。”

translations.literal: Your subject disgraces the office of censors and dare not carry out the order."
translations.idiomatic: Your subject disgraces the office of censors and dare not carry out the order."

sentences.zh: 太宗意解，仁軌竟免。

translations.literal: The Emperor's mind softened, and Rengui was ultimately spared.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor's mind softened, and Rengui was ultimately spared.

sentences.zh: 乾祐尋遷侍御史。

translations.literal: Qianyou was soon promoted to attendant censor.
translations.idiomatic: Qianyou was soon promoted to attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 母卒，廬於墓側，負土成墳，太宗遣使就墓弔之，仍旌表其門。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he lived in a hut beside her tomb and carried earth to build the mound. Taizong sent an envoy to mourn at the tomb and also granted an honorific gate tablet to his household.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, he lived in a hut beside her tomb and carried earth to build the mound. Taizong sent an envoy to mourn at the tomb and also granted an honorific gate tablet to his household.

sentences.zh: 後歷長安令、治書御史，皆有能名，擢拜御史大夫。

translations.literal: Later he successively held the posts of magistrate of Chang'an and reviewing censor, winning a reputation for ability in each, and was raised to Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Later he successively held the posts of magistrate of Chang'an and reviewing censor, winning a reputation for ability in each, and was raised to Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 乾祐與中書令褚遂良不協，竟為遂良所構。

translations.literal: Qianyou did not get along with Chief Minister Chu Suiliang and was ultimately framed by Suiliang.
translations.idiomatic: Qianyou did not get along with Chief Minister Chu Suiliang and was ultimately framed by Suiliang.

sentences.zh: 永徽初，繼受邢、魏等州刺史。

translations.literal: In the early Yonghui era, he successively received appointment as prefect of Xing, Wei, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Yonghui era, he successively received appointment as prefect of Xing, Wei, and other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 乾祐雖強直有器幹，而昵於小人，既典外郡，與令史結友，書疏往返，令伺朝廷之事。

translations.literal: Although Qianyou was forceful, upright, and capable, he was close to petty men; once he governed outer prefectures, he made friends with clerks and exchanged letters back and forth, having them spy on court affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Although Qianyou was forceful, upright, and capable, he was close to petty men; once he governed outer prefectures, he made friends with clerks and exchanged letters back and forth, having them spy on court affairs.

sentences.zh: 俄為友人所發，坐流愛州。

translations.literal: Before long he was exposed by a friend and was punished by exile to Aizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was exposed by a friend and was punished by exile to Aizhou.

sentences.zh: 乾封中，起為桂州都督，歷拜司刑太常伯。

translations.literal: During the Qianfeng era he was recalled as military governor of Guizhou and successively appointed Minister of Justice and Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qianfeng era he was recalled as military governor of Guizhou and successively appointed Minister of Justice and Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 舉京兆功曹參軍崔擢為尚書郎，事既不果，私以告擢。

translations.literal: He recommended Cui Zhuo, records officer of Jingzhao, for a post in the Secretariat; when the matter did not succeed, he privately told Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended Cui Zhuo, records officer of Jingzhao, for a post in the Secretariat; when the matter did not succeed, he privately told Zhuo.

sentences.zh: 後擢有犯，乃告乾祐泄禁中語以贖罪，乾祐復坐免官。

translations.literal: Later when Zhuo committed an offense, he reported that Qianyou had leaked palace secrets to atone for his crime, and Qianyou was again punished and dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Later when Zhuo committed an offense, he reported that Qianyou had leaked palace secrets to atone for his crime, and Qianyou was again punished and dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: He soon died.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died.

sentences.zh: 昭德，即乾祐之孽子也。

translations.literal: Zhaode was the illegitimate son of Qianyou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaode was the illegitimate son of Qianyou.

sentences.zh: 強幹有父風。

translations.literal: Forceful and capable, he had his father's spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Forceful and capable, he had his father's spirit.

sentences.zh: 少舉明經，累遷至鳳閣侍郎。

translations.literal: In youth he passed the Mingjing examination and rose through promotions to Vice Director of the Fengge Department.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he passed the Mingjing examination and rose through promotions to Vice Director of the Fengge Department.

sentences.zh: 長壽二年，增置夏官侍郎三員，時選昭德與婁師德、侯知一為之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Changshou, three additional vice directors of the Ministry of War were created; at the time Zhaode was chosen along with Lou Deshi and Hou Zhiyi.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Changshou, three additional vice directors of the Ministry of War were created; at the time Zhaode was chosen along with Lou Deshi and Hou Zhiyi.

sentences.zh: 是歲，又遷鳳閣鸞台平章事，尋加檢校內史。

translations.literal: That same year he was further made Co-Director of the Fengge and Luantai departments, and soon given the additional title of Acting Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: That same year he was further made Co-Director of the Fengge and Luantai departments, and soon given the additional title of Acting Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 長壽中，神都改作文昌台及定鼎、上東諸門，又城外郭，皆昭德創其制度，時人以為能。

translations.literal: During Changshou, when the Divine Capital was rebuilt as the Wenchang Terrace and the Dingding, Shangdong, and other gates, as well as the outer city wall, Zhaode devised their designs in each case, and people of the time regarded him as capable.
translations.idiomatic: During Changshou, when the Divine Capital was rebuilt as the Wenchang Terrace and the Dingding, Shangdong, and other gates, as well as the outer city wall, Zhaode devised their designs in each case, and people of the time regarded him as capable.

sentences.zh: 初，都城洛水天津之東，立德坊西南隅，有中橋及利涉橋，以通行李。

translations.literal: Initially, east of the Luo River at Tianjin in the capital, at the southwest corner of Lide Ward, there were the Zhong Bridge and the Lishe Bridge for passing traffic and luggage.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, east of the Luo River at Tianjin in the capital, at the southwest corner of Lide Ward, there were the Zhong Bridge and the Lishe Bridge for passing traffic and luggage.

sentences.zh: 上元中，司農卿韋機始移中橋置於安眾坊之左街，當長夏門，都人甚以為便，因廢利涉橋，所省萬計。

translations.literal: During Shangyuan, Minister of Public Works Wei Ji first moved the Zhong Bridge to the left street of Anzhong Ward, facing Changxia Gate; the people of the capital greatly found this convenient, and the Lishe Bridge was therefore abolished, saving tens of thousands in expense.
translations.idiomatic: During Shangyuan, Minister of Public Works Wei Ji first moved the Zhong Bridge to the left street of Anzhong Ward, facing Changxia Gate; the people of the capital greatly found this convenient, and the Lishe Bridge was therefore abolished, saving tens of thousands in expense.

sentences.zh: 然歲為洛水衝注，常勞治葺。

translations.literal: Yet each year the Luo River rushed against it, and repair was constantly needed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet each year the Luo River rushed against it, and repair was constantly needed.

sentences.zh: 昭德創意積石為腳，銳其前以分水勢，自是竟無漂損。

translations.literal: Zhaode devised piling stones as piers and sharpening their fronts to divide the force of the water; from then on there was no drifting damage at all.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaode devised piling stones as piers and sharpening their fronts to divide the force of the water; from then on there was no drifting damage at all.

sentences.zh: 時則天以武承嗣為文昌左相，昭德密奏曰：“承嗣，陛下之侄，又是親王，不宜更在機權，以惑眾庶。

translations.literal: At the time Empress Wu had made Wu Chengsi Left Chancellor of the Wenchang Department. Zhaode secretly memorialized: "Chengsi is Your Majesty's nephew and also a prince of the blood—he ought not to hold further control of critical power, lest he mislead the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Empress Wu had made Wu Chengsi Left Chancellor of the Wenchang Department. Zhaode secretly memorialized: "Chengsi is Your Majesty's nephew and also a prince of the blood—he ought not to hold further control of critical power, lest he mislead the multitude.

sentences.zh: 且自古帝王，父子之間猶相篡奪，況在姑侄，豈得委權與之？

translations.literal: Moreover, from antiquity emperors and kings have even among father and son seized power from one another—how much the more so between aunt and nephew? How can power be entrusted to him?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, from antiquity emperors and kings have even among father and son seized power from one another—how much the more so between aunt and nephew? How can power be entrusted to him?

sentences.zh: 脫若乘便，寶位寧可安乎？”

translations.literal: If he should seize the opportunity, could the imperial throne remain secure?"
translations.idiomatic: If he should seize the opportunity, could the imperial throne remain secure?"

sentences.zh: 則天矍然曰：“我未之思也。”

translations.literal: Empress Wu started and said: "I had not thought of this."
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu started and said: "I had not thought of this."

sentences.zh: 承嗣亦嚐返譖昭德，則天曰：“自我任昭德，每獲高臥，是代我勞苦，非汝所及也。”

translations.literal: Chengsi also on occasion slandered Zhaode in return. Empress Wu said: "Since I put Zhaode in office, I can always rest at ease—he takes my burdens upon himself. That is beyond your reach."
translations.idiomatic: Chengsi also on occasion slandered Zhaode in return. Empress Wu said: "Since I put Zhaode in office, I can always rest at ease—he takes my burdens upon himself. That is beyond your reach."

sentences.zh: 承嗣俄轉太子少保，罷知政事。

translations.literal: Chengsi was soon transferred to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and removed from managing state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Chengsi was soon transferred to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and removed from managing state affairs.

sentences.zh: 延載初，鳳閣舍人張嘉福令洛陽人王慶之率輕薄惡少數百人詣闕上表，請立武承嗣為皇太子。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yanzai, Palace Secretary Zhang Jiafu had the Luoyang man Wang Qingzhi lead several hundred frivolous young ruffians to the palace to submit a memorial asking that Wu Chengsi be made Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yanzai, Palace Secretary Zhang Jiafu had the Luoyang man Wang Qingzhi lead several hundred frivolous young ruffians to the palace to submit a memorial asking that Wu Chengsi be made Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 則天不許，慶之固請不已，則天令昭德詰責之，令散。

translations.literal: Empress Wu did not permit it. Qingzhi pressed his request without cease, and Empress Wu ordered Zhaode to interrogate and rebuke him and have the crowd dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu did not permit it. Qingzhi pressed his request without cease, and Empress Wu ordered Zhaode to interrogate and rebuke him and have the crowd dispersed.

sentences.zh: 昭德便杖殺慶之，餘眾乃息。

translations.literal: Zhaode immediately had Qingzhi beaten to death, and the rest of the crowd then subsided.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaode immediately had Qingzhi beaten to death, and the rest of the crowd then subsided.

sentences.zh: 昭德因奏曰：“臣聞文武之道，布在方策，民有侄為天子而為姑立廟乎！

translations.literal: Zhaode then memorialized: "Your subject has heard that the way of Wen and Wu is spread in the written records—is there any people whose nephew became Son of Heaven yet built a temple for his aunt?
translations.idiomatic: Zhaode then memorialized: "Your subject has heard that the way of Wen and Wu is spread in the written records—is there any people whose nephew became Son of Heaven yet built a temple for his aunt?

sentences.zh: 以親親言之，則天皇是陛下夫也，皇嗣是陛下子也，陛下正合傳之子孫，為萬代計。

translations.literal: Speaking in terms of kinship, the Heavenly Emperor was Your Majesty's husband, and the imperial heir is Your Majesty's son. Your Majesty should properly transmit the throne to your sons and grandsons for the planning of ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: Speaking in terms of kinship, the Heavenly Emperor was Your Majesty's husband, and the imperial heir is Your Majesty's son. Your Majesty should properly transmit the throne to your sons and grandsons for the planning of ten thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 況陛下承天皇顧托而有天下，若立承嗣，臣恐天皇不血食矣。”

translations.literal: Moreover, Your Majesty received the realm through the Heavenly Emperor's dying trust; if Chengsi were established as heir, your subject fears the Heavenly Emperor would receive no sacrificial offerings of blood."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Your Majesty received the realm through the Heavenly Emperor's dying trust; if Chengsi were established as heir, your subject fears the Heavenly Emperor would receive no sacrificial offerings of blood."

sentences.zh: 則天寤之，乃止。

translations.literal: Empress Wu awoke to this and stopped the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu awoke to this and stopped the matter.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷諛佞者多獲進用，故幸恩者，事無大小，但近諂諛，皆獲進見。

translations.literal: At the time many flatterers in court were promoted, so those who sought favor, regardless of the matter's size, need only draw near with flattery to gain an audience.
translations.idiomatic: At the time many flatterers in court were promoted, so those who sought favor, regardless of the matter's size, need only draw near with flattery to gain an audience.

sentences.zh: 有人於洛水中獲白石數點赤，詣闕輒進。

translations.literal: Someone obtained white stones from the Luo River with several red specks and, on reaching the palace, promptly presented them.
translations.idiomatic: Someone obtained white stones from the Luo River with several red specks and, on reaching the palace, promptly presented them.

sentences.zh: 諸宰相詰之，對云：“此石赤心，所以來進。”

translations.literal: The chief ministers questioned him. He replied: "This stone has a red heart—that is why I come to present it."
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers questioned him. He replied: "This stone has a red heart—that is why I come to present it."

sentences.zh: 昭德叱之曰：“此石赤心，洛水中餘石豈能盡反耶？”

translations.literal: Zhaode rebuked him: "This stone has a red heart—are all the other stones in the Luo River supposed to turn traitor?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhaode rebuked him: "So this stone has a loyal red heart—must every other stone in the Luo River be a traitor too?"

sentences.zh: 左右皆笑。

translations.literal: Those on both sides all laughed.
translations.idiomatic: Those on both sides all laughed.

sentences.zh: 是時，來俊臣、侯思止等枉撓刑法，誣陷忠良，人皆懾懼，昭德每廷奏其狀，由是俊臣黨與少自摧屈。

translations.literal: At this time Lai Junchen, Hou Sizhi, and others perverted the law, falsely implicating the loyal and good, and everyone was fearful. Zhaode repeatedly presented their abuses at court, and thereby the faction of Junchen was somewhat humbled.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Lai Junchen, Hou Sizhi, and others perverted the law, falsely implicating the loyal and good, and everyone was fearful. Zhaode repeatedly presented their abuses at court, and thereby the faction of Junchen was somewhat humbled.

sentences.zh: 來俊臣又嚐棄故妻而娶太原王慶詵女，侯思止亦奏娶趙郡李自挹女，敕政事堂共商量。

translations.literal: Lai Junchen also once abandoned his former wife and married the daughter of Wang Qingyu of Taiyuan. Hou Sizhi likewise memorialized to marry the daughter of Li Ziyi of Zhao Commandery. An edict ordered the chief ministers to discuss it together.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Junchen also once abandoned his former wife and married the daughter of Wang Qingyu of Taiyuan. Hou Sizhi likewise memorialized to marry the daughter of Li Ziyi of Zhao Commandery. An edict ordered the chief ministers to discuss it together.

sentences.zh: 昭德撫掌謂諸宰相曰：“大可笑！

translations.literal: Zhaode clapped his hands and said to the chief ministers: "Utterly laughable!
translations.idiomatic: Zhaode clapped his hands and said to the chief ministers: "Utterly laughable!

sentences.zh: 往年俊臣賊劫王慶詵女，已大辱國。

translations.literal: In past years Junchen robbed Wang Qingyu's daughter like a bandit—a great dishonor to the state.
translations.idiomatic: In past years Junchen robbed Wang Qingyu's daughter like a bandit—a great dishonor to the state.

sentences.zh: 今日此奴又請索李自挹女，無乃復辱國耶！”

translations.literal: Today this slave again asks for Li Ziyi's daughter—is the state not to be dishonored once more!"
translations.idiomatic: Today this slave again asks for Li Ziyi's daughter—is the state not to be dishonored once more!"

sentences.zh: 尋奏寢之。

translations.literal: He soon memorialized and the matter was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: He soon memorialized and the matter was shelved.

sentences.zh: 侯思止後竟為昭德所繩，搒殺之。

translations.literal: Hou Sizhi was later bound by Zhaode after all and beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Sizhi was later bound by Zhaode after all and beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 既而昭德專權用事，頗為朝野所惡。

translations.literal: Before long Zhaode monopolized power and managed affairs, and was greatly disliked by court and countryside alike.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Zhaode monopolized power and managed affairs, and was greatly disliked by court and countryside alike.

sentences.zh: 前魯王府功曹參軍丘愔上疏言其罪狀曰：

translations.literal: Qiu Yin, former records officer of the Prince of Lu's household, submitted a memorial stating his crimes, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Yin, former records officer of the Prince of Lu's household, submitted a memorial stating his crimes, saying:

sentences.zh: 臣聞百王之失，皆由權歸於下。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that the failures of the hundred kings all came from power returning to those below.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject has heard that the failures of the hundred kings all came from power returning to those below.

sentences.zh: 宰臣持政，常以勢盛為殃。

translations.literal: When chief ministers hold power, excessive strength often becomes a calamity.
translations.idiomatic: When chief ministers hold power, excessive strength often becomes a calamity.

sentences.zh: 魏冉誅庶族以安秦，非不忠也。

translations.literal: Wei Ran executed the collateral clan to secure Qin—not because he was disloyal.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Ran executed the collateral clan to secure Qin—not because he was disloyal.

sentences.zh: 弱諸侯以強國，亦有功也。

translations.literal: Weakening the feudal lords to strengthen the state also had merit.
translations.idiomatic: Weakening the feudal lords to strengthen the state also had merit.

sentences.zh: 然以出入自專，擊斷無忌，威震人主，不聞有王，張祿一進深言，卒用憂死。

translations.literal: Yet because he came and went at his own discretion, struck and judged without restraint, his awesomeness shook the ruler, and the king heard no one—Zhang Lu once advanced deep counsel, and in the end Wei Ran died of worry.
translations.idiomatic: Yet because he came and went at his own discretion, struck and judged without restraint, his awesomeness shook the ruler, and the king heard no one—Zhang Lu once advanced deep counsel, and in the end Wei Ran died of worry.

sentences.zh: 向使昭王不即覺悟，魏冉果以專權，則秦之霸業，或不傳其子孫。

translations.literal: If King Zhao had not quickly awakened, and Wei Ran had indeed monopolized power, then Qin's hegemony might not have passed to his descendants.
translations.idiomatic: If King Zhao had not quickly awakened, and Wei Ran had indeed monopolized power, then Qin's hegemony might not have passed to his descendants.

sentences.zh: 陛下創業興王，撥亂英主，總權收柄，司契握圖。

translations.literal: Your Majesty founded the enterprise and raised the throne, a heroic ruler who quelled disorder, gathering all power and seizing the reins, holding the tally and grasping the map.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty founded the enterprise and raised the throne, a heroic ruler who quelled disorder, gathering all power and seizing the reins, holding the tally and grasping the map.

sentences.zh: 天授已前，萬機獨斷，發命皆中，舉事無遺，公卿百僚，具職而已。

translations.literal: Before Tianshou, you alone decided the myriad affairs; every order hit the mark, every undertaking was complete, and the high officials and hundred ranks merely fulfilled their duties.
translations.idiomatic: Before Tianshou, you alone decided the myriad affairs; every order hit the mark, every undertaking was complete, and the high officials and hundred ranks merely fulfilled their duties.

sentences.zh: 自長壽已來，厭怠細政，委任昭德，使掌機權。

translations.literal: Since Changshou you have wearied of detailed government and entrusted Zhaode, making him hold critical power.
translations.idiomatic: Since Changshou you have wearied of detailed government and entrusted Zhaode, making him hold critical power.

sentences.zh: 然其幹濟小才，不堪軍國大用。

translations.literal: Yet his talent for practical management is small; he cannot bear great use in military and state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his talent for practical management is small; he cannot bear great use in military and state affairs.

sentences.zh: 直以性好淩轢，氣負剛強，盲聾下人，芻狗同列，刻薄慶賞，矯枉憲章，國家所賴者微，所妨者大。

translations.literal: It is simply that by nature he likes to bully and humiliate; his spirit relies on stubborn force; he deafens and blinds his subordinates and treats colleagues like straw dogs; he is harsh in rewards and punishments and twists the statutes—what the state may rely on from him is slight, what he obstructs is great.
translations.idiomatic: It is simply that by nature he likes to bully and humiliate; his spirit relies on stubborn force; he deafens and blinds his subordinates and treats colleagues like straw dogs; he is harsh in rewards and punishments and twists the statutes—what the state may rely on from him is slight, what he obstructs is great.

sentences.zh: 天下杜口，莫敢一言，聲威翕赫，日已熾盛。

translations.literal: Under Heaven mouths are sealed; none dare speak a word. His renown and power blaze ever more fiercely day by day.
translations.idiomatic: Under Heaven mouths are sealed; none dare speak a word. His renown and power blaze ever more fiercely day by day.

sentences.zh: 臣近於南台見敕日，諸處奏事，陛下已依，昭德請不依，陛下便不依。

translations.literal: Your subject recently at the Southern Censorate saw an edict-day document: on memorials from all quarters, when Your Majesty had already approved, if Zhaode asked that they not be approved, Your Majesty then did not approve.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject recently at the Southern Censorate saw an edict-day document: on memorials from all quarters, when Your Majesty had already approved, if Zhaode asked that they not be approved, Your Majesty then did not approve.

sentences.zh: 如此改張，不可勝數。

translations.literal: Such reversals are beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Such reversals are beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 昭德參奉機密，獻可替否，事有便利，不預諮謀，要待畫旨將行，方始別生駁異。

translations.literal: Zhaode participates in confidential matters and should offer approval or dissent—but when something is expedient, he does not consult beforehand; he waits until the imperial decision is marked and about to be executed, then raises separate objections.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaode participates in confidential matters and should offer approval or dissent—but when something is expedient, he does not consult beforehand; he waits until the imperial decision is marked and about to be executed, then raises separate objections.

sentences.zh: 揚露專擅，顯示於人，歸美引愆，義不如此。

translations.literal: To expose one's monopoly and display it before others, taking credit while shifting blame—that is not how duty should be done.
translations.idiomatic: To expose one's monopoly and display it before others, taking credit while shifting blame—that is not how duty should be done.

sentences.zh: 州縣列位，台寺庶官，入謁出辭，望塵習氣。

translations.literal: Prefectural and county officials in rank, clerks and officials of the bureaus—coming to audience and taking leave, all caught his dust and breathed his air.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural and county officials, bureau clerks, and staff of every rank—entering audience and taking leave—all bowed to his shadow and breathed his air.

sentences.zh: 一切奏讞，與奪事宜，皆承旨意，附會上言。

translations.literal: All memorials and legal opinions, all decisions of grant and denial, follow his intent and echo it upward.
translations.idiomatic: All memorials and legal opinions, all decisions of grant and denial, follow his intent and echo it upward.

sentences.zh: 今有秩之吏，多為昭德之人。

translations.literal: Now most officials of rank are Zhaode's men.
translations.idiomatic: Now most officials of rank are Zhaode's men.

sentences.zh: 陛下勿謂昭德小心，是我手臂。

translations.literal: Your Majesty must not think Zhaode is careful—that he is my arms.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty must not think Zhaode is careful—that he is my arms.

sentences.zh: 臣觀其膽，乃大於身，鼻息所衝，上拂雲漢。

translations.literal: Your subject observes that his gall is larger than his body; where his breath strikes, it brushes the Milky Way on high.
translations.idiomatic: I see that his arrogance outgrows his body; his very breath seems to brush the Milky Way.

sentences.zh: 近者新陷來、張兩族，兼挫侯、王二仇，鋒銳理不可當，方寸良難窺測。

translations.literal: Recently he newly ruined the Lai and Zhang clans and also humbled his enemies Hou and Wang; his edge is sharp and cannot be withstood, and his inmost mind is truly hard to fathom.
translations.idiomatic: Recently he newly ruined the Lai and Zhang clans and also humbled his enemies Hou and Wang; his edge is sharp and cannot be withstood, and his inmost mind is truly hard to fathom.

sentences.zh: 書曰：知人亦未易，人亦未易知。

translations.literal: The Documents say: To know men is not easy, and men are not easy to know.
translations.idiomatic: The Documents say: To know men is not easy, and men are not easy to know.

sentences.zh: 漢光武將寵龐萌，可以托孤，卒為戎首。

translations.literal: Emperor Guangwu of Han was about to favor Pang Meng and trust him with his orphan heir, yet Pang ended as leader of rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangwu of Han was about to favor Pang Meng and trust him with his orphan heir, yet Pang ended as leader of rebellion.

sentences.zh: 魏明帝期司馬懿以安國，竟肆奸回。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming of Wei looked to Sima Yi to secure the state, yet Yi in the end indulged treachery and deceit.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming of Wei looked to Sima Yi to secure the state, yet Yi in the end indulged treachery and deceit.

sentences.zh: 夫小家治生，有千百之資，將以托人，尚憂失授。

translations.literal: For a small household managing its livelihood, with a few hundred or thousand in assets, when about to entrust them to someone, one still fears making the wrong choice.
translations.idiomatic: Even a small household with a few hundred or thousand in savings, about to entrust its fortune to another, still fears choosing the wrong man.

sentences.zh: 況兼天下之重，而可輕忽委任者乎！

translations.literal: How much more when the weight of all under Heaven is involved—can one lightly and carelessly entrust it!
translations.idiomatic: How much more when the weight of the empire is at stake—can such power be entrusted lightly!

sentences.zh: 今昭德作福專威，橫絕朝野，愛憎與奪，旁若無人。

translations.literal: Now Zhaode makes blessings and monopolizes authority, cutting across court and countryside; in granting love or hate, giving or taking away, he acts as though no one else were beside him.
translations.idiomatic: Today Zhaode monopolizes favor and power, towering over court and countryside, dispensing rewards and punishments as though no one else existed.

sentences.zh: 陛下恩遇至深，蔽過甚厚。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's gracious treatment of him runs very deep, and the covering of his faults is very thick.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty favors him deeply and shields his faults generously.

sentences.zh: 臣聞蟻穴壞堤，針芒寫氣，涓涓不絕，必成江河。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that an ant hole ruins a dike, a needle point vents breath, and trickles that do not cease must become rivers.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that an ant hole can ruin a dike, a needle prick can drain strength, and trickles that never stop become rivers.

sentences.zh: 履霜堅冰，須防其漸，權重一去，收之極難。

translations.literal: Treading frost leads to solid ice; one must guard against gradual growth. Once heavy power is gone forth, to take it back is extremely hard.
translations.idiomatic: Tread on frost and solid ice follows—guard against things while they are still small. Once great power slips away, it is almost impossible to reclaim.

sentences.zh: 臣又聞輕議近臣，犯顏深諫，明君聖主，亦有不容。

translations.literal: Your subject has also heard that lightly discussing a close minister, risking one's face in deep remonstrance—even enlightened rulers and sage sovereigns sometimes do not tolerate it.
translations.idiomatic: I also know that to speak lightly of a close minister and risk one's life in blunt remonstrance—even enlightened rulers sometimes will not bear it.

sentences.zh: 臣熟知今日言之於前，明日伏誅於後。

translations.literal: Your subject knows full well that speaking today before the throne, tomorrow one may be executed lying prostrate.
translations.idiomatic: I know well that what I say today may bring execution tomorrow.

sentences.zh: 但使國安身死，臣實不悔。

translations.literal: Yet if the state is secure though your subject dies, he truly will not regret it.
translations.idiomatic: Yet if the realm is secure though I die, I shall not regret it.

sentences.zh: 陛下深覽臣言，為萬姓自愛。

translations.literal: May Your Majesty deeply peruse your subject's words and, for the sake of the myriad people, cherish yourself.
translations.idiomatic: May Your Majesty weigh my words deeply and, for the sake of the people, guard yourself.

sentences.zh: 時長上果毅鄧注又著《碩論》數千言，備述昭德專權之狀，鳳閣舍人逢弘敏遽奏其論。

translations.literal: At that time the senior commander of the Changshang guard Deng Zhu also composed a Great Discourse of several thousand words, fully describing Zhaode's monopoly of power, and the drafting officer of the Phoenix Pavilion Feng Hongmin hurriedly submitted his treatise.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Senior Commander Deng Zhu also wrote a lengthy Great Discourse detailing Zhaode's monopoly of power, and drafting officer Feng Hongmin quickly submitted it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 則天乃惡昭德，謂納言姚璹曰：“昭德身為內史，備荷殊榮，誠如所言，實負於國。”

translations.literal: Zetian then came to dislike Zhaode and said to Counselor Yao Shuo: "Zhaode personally served as Director of the Secretariat and received extraordinary honor; if what is said is true, he has truly failed the state."
translations.idiomatic: Zetian then turned against Zhaode and told Counselor Yao Shuo: "Zhaode served as director of the Secretariat and received extraordinary honor. If what they say is true, he has truly betrayed the state."

sentences.zh: 延載初，左遷欽州南賓尉，數日，又命免死配流。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yanzai he was demoted to defender of Nanbin in Qin Prefecture; after several days he was again ordered spared death but sentenced to exile.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Yanzai he was demoted to defender of Nanbin in Qin Prefecture. Within days he was spared execution but sentenced to exile.

sentences.zh: 尋又召拜監察御史。

translations.literal: Soon he was again summoned and appointed investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was summoned back and appointed investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 時太僕少卿來俊臣與昭德素不協，乃誣構昭德有逆謀，因被下獄，與來俊臣同日而誅。

translations.literal: At that time the vice minister of the imperial stud Lai Junchen had long been at odds with Zhaode; he therefore framed Zhaode for plotting rebellion, and so Zhaode was cast into prison and executed on the same day as Lai Junchen.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud Lai Junchen had long been at odds with Zhaode and framed him for treason. Zhaode was thrown into prison and executed on the same day as Lai Junchen.

sentences.zh: 是日大雨，士庶莫不痛昭德而慶俊臣也。

translations.literal: That day there was heavy rain; gentry and commoners all grieved for Zhaode and rejoiced at Junchen's fate.
translations.idiomatic: That day a great rain fell, and scholars and commoners alike mourned Zhaode and rejoiced at Junchen's death.

sentences.zh: 相謂曰：“今日天雨，可謂一悲一喜矣。”

translations.literal: They said to one another: "Today's rain from Heaven may be called one grief and one joy."
translations.idiomatic: People said to one another: "Heaven weeps today—one sorrow and one joy together."

sentences.zh: 神龍中，降制曰：“故李昭德勤恪在公，強直自達。

translations.literal: In the Shenlong era an edict was issued, saying: "The late Li Zhaode was diligent and respectful in public service and strong and upright in making himself heard.
translations.idiomatic: In the Shenlong era an edict declared: "The late Li Zhaode was diligent in public service and forthright in making himself heard.

sentences.zh: 立朝正色，不吐剛以茹柔；

translations.literal: Standing in court with stern countenance, he would not yield his firmness to swallow what was soft;
translations.idiomatic: He stood in court with stern dignity and would not trade his firmness for flattery;

sentences.zh: 當軸勵詞，必抗情以歷詆。

translations.literal: when at the hub he urged his words, he always resisted sentiment to go through with denunciation.
translations.idiomatic: when he held power he spoke boldly and always resisted pressure to denounce others unjustly.

sentences.zh: 墉隍府寺，樹勣良多，變更規模，歿而不朽。

translations.literal: In walls, moats, offices, and temples he planted many achievements; in changing plans and models, though dead he is not forgotten.
translations.idiomatic: In walls, moats, offices, and temples he left many achievements; the plans he changed endure though he is gone.

sentences.zh: 道淪福善，業虧嫉惡，名級不追，風流將沫。

translations.literal: The Way was lost and blessings to the good failed; his work was marred by jealous hatred of evil; rank and title were not pursued, and his renown is about to fade.
translations.idiomatic: Fortune failed the good man, jealous enemies marred his work, no posthumous rank was granted, and his renown nearly faded away.

sentences.zh: 式旌壞樹，光被幽明，可贈左御史大夫。”

translations.literal: Let a broken tree be marked in honor; may his light reach the hidden and the manifest—he may be posthumously granted the post of Left Censor-in-Chief."
translations.idiomatic: Let him be honored though his tree is broken; may his light reach both the living and the dead—he is posthumously to be made Left Censor-in-Chief."

sentences.zh: 德宗建中三年，加贈司空。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianzhong under Emperor Dezong he was further posthumously granted the post of Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jianzhong, Emperor Dezong further posthumously made him Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：裴炎位居相輔，時屬艱難，歷覽前蹤，非無忠節。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Pei Yan stood in the rank of chief minister at a time of hardship; reviewing his earlier traces, he was not without loyal integrity.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Pei Yan served as chief minister in a time of hardship. Looking back on his career, he was not without loyal integrity.

sentences.zh: 但見遲而慮淺，又遭命以會時。

translations.literal: Yet he was seen to be slow and shallow in counsel, and again met his fate as the times required.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was slow to act and shallow in judgment, and fate caught him at the wrong moment.

sentences.zh: 何者，當是時，高宗晏駕尚新，武氏革命未見，炎也唯慮中宗之過失，是其淺也；

translations.literal: Why? At that time Gaozong's death was still recent and Wu's revolution had not yet appeared; Yan only worried over Zhongzong's faults—that was his shallowness;
translations.idiomatic: Why? At that time Gaozong had only recently died and Wu's seizure of power was not yet plain. Yan worried only about Zhongzong's faults—that was his shallowness.

sentences.zh: 不見太后之苞藏。

translations.literal: he did not see the Empress Dowager's hidden designs.
translations.idiomatic: He failed to see the Empress Dowager's hidden designs.

sentences.zh: 是其遲也。

translations.literal: That was his slowness.
translations.idiomatic: That was his slowness.

sentences.zh: 及乎承嗣請封祖禰，三思勸殺宗親，然後徒有諫章，何嘗濟事，是辜遺托，豈痛伏誅。

translations.literal: Only when Chengsi requested enfeoffment of ancestors and Sansi urged killing the imperial kin did he then merely have remonstrance memorials—when had they ever helped affairs? He betrayed the dying charge—was it painful that he was executed lying prostrate?
translations.idiomatic: Only when Chengsi sought to ennoble his ancestors and Sansi urged killing the imperial kin did he offer remonstrance—and what good did it do? He betrayed the late emperor's trust. Was it any wonder he was executed?

sentences.zh: 時論則然，遲淺須信。

translations.literal: Contemporary opinion was thus; his slowness and shallowness must be believed.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporary opinion says as much, and his slowness and shallowness are credible.

sentences.zh: 況聞睹構逆則示其閑暇，俾殺降則彰彼猜嫌，小數有餘，大度何足，又其驗也。

translations.literal: Moreover, hearing of rebellion he showed leisure; causing surrendered enemies to be killed he displayed suspicion; in petty calculation he had surplus, in great breadth he was insufficient—this too is proof.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when rebellion arose he showed unconcern; when surrendered enemies were killed he revealed his jealousy. He was clever in small matters but lacked great breadth—that too is proof.

sentences.zh: 禕之名父之子，諒知其才，著述頗精，履歷無愧。

translations.literal: Yizhi was the son of a famed father; it may be assumed his talent was known; his writings were quite refined and his career without shame.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhi was the son of a famous father, and his talent was well known. His writings were polished and his career unblemished.

sentences.zh: 師範王府，秉執相權，咸有能名，固愜群議。

translations.literal: He taught and modeled the princely household and held chief ministerial power; in all he had a reputation for ability and truly satisfied public opinion.
translations.idiomatic: He tutored the princely household and wielded ministerial power, winning a reputation for ability that satisfied public opinion.

sentences.zh: 何乃失言於大隱，取金於萬榮，潛見內人，私通嬖妾，使濁跡玷其清譽，淫行汙於貞名。

translations.literal: Why then did he misspeak to Dayin, take gold from Wanrong, secretly see inner attendants, and have private dealings with a favorite concubine, so that muddy traces stained his clear reputation and licentious conduct defiled his chaste name?
translations.idiomatic: Why then did he speak rashly to Dayin, take gold from Wanrong, secretly visit palace women, and consort with a favorite concubine, staining his clean reputation and defiling his upright name?

sentences.zh: 若言俗困濫刑，公行誣告，即又自昧周防之道，人非盡戮之冤。

translations.literal: If one says the custom was troubled by excessive punishment and public false accusations, then he himself was also blind to the way of thorough precaution, and men were not all victims of unjust slaughter.
translations.idiomatic: If one says the age suffered from excessive punishment and false accusations, he himself ignored prudent self-defense, and not every man executed was innocent of him.

sentences.zh: 賜死於家，猶為多幸，臨終不撓，抑又徒勞。

translations.literal: To be granted death at home was still great fortune; to be unbending at the end was again vain effort.
translations.idiomatic: Death by imperial gift at home was still a mercy; his unyielding at the end was vain pride.

sentences.zh: 玄同富於詞學，公任權衡，當為典選之時，備疏擇才之理。

translations.literal: Xuantong was rich in literary learning and openly entrusted with the scales of office; at the time when he should have presided over selection, he fully set forth the principles of choosing talent.
translations.idiomatic: Xuantong was learned in letters and held public office. When he should have directed personnel selection, he laid out the principles of choosing talent in full.

sentences.zh: 但以高宗棄代之後，則天居位之間，革命是懷，附己為愛，苟一言之不順，則赤族以難逃。

translations.literal: But after Gaozong abandoned his generation and while Zetian held position, revolution was in her heart and favoring herself was her love; if a single word did not accord, then extinction of the clan was hard to escape.
translations.idiomatic: But after Gaozong's death, while Zetian held power, she sought revolution and loved only those who sided with her. One disloyal word could bring extinction to an entire clan.

sentences.zh: 是以唐之名臣，難忘中興之計；

translations.literal: Therefore Tang's famed ministers could not forget plans for restoration;
translations.idiomatic: Thus Tang's great ministers could not forget plans to restore the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 周之酷吏，常謀並進之讒。

translations.literal: Zhou's cruel officials constantly plotted slander to advance together.
translations.idiomatic: While Wu's cruel officials constantly plotted mutual advancement through slander.

sentences.zh: 玄同欲復皇儲，固宜難免，死而無過，人殺何妨。

translations.literal: Xuantong wished to restore the imperial heir—naturally he could hardly escape; in death he had no fault—what harm if men killed him?
translations.idiomatic: Xuantong wished to restore the heir apparent and naturally could not escape punishment. He died without fault—what matter if men killed him?

sentences.zh: 昭德強幹為臣，機巧蒞事，凡所製置，動有規模。

translations.literal: Zhaode was strong and capable as a minister, clever and resourceful in handling affairs; whatever he established or arranged always had pattern and scale.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaode was a forceful, capable minister, clever in affairs; whatever he undertook was done on a planned scale.

sentences.zh: 武承嗣方持左相權，將立為皇太子，尋更所任，復寢其謀，咸由昭德之言，能拒則天之旨。

translations.literal: Wu Chengsi was then holding the power of left chief minister and was about to be made heir apparent; soon his appointment was changed and the plot again put to rest—all through Zhaode's words, able to refuse Zetian's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Chengsi then held power as left chief minister and was nearly made heir apparent, but his appointment was soon changed and the plot shelved—all because Zhaode's words could resist Zetian's intent.

sentences.zh: 又觀其誅侯思止，法王慶之，挫來俊臣，致朋黨漸衰，諛佞稍退。

translations.literal: Again, observe that he executed Hou Sizhi, punished Wang Qingzhi by law, checked Lai Junchen, and caused factional cliques gradually to decline and flatterers slightly to retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Observe too that he executed Hou Sizhi, punished Wang Qingzhi, checked Lai Junchen, and caused factions to weaken and flatterers to retreat.

sentences.zh: 又則天謂承嗣曰：“我任昭德，每獲高臥，代我勞苦，非汝所及也。”

translations.literal: Again Zetian said to Chengsi: "When I put Zhaode in office I can always rest at ease; he takes my labor and hardship upon himself—that is beyond your reach."
translations.idiomatic: Zetian also told Chengsi: "When I put Zhaode in office I can rest at ease. He bears my burdens—something beyond your reach."

sentences.zh: 此則強幹機巧之驗焉。

translations.literal: This then is proof of his strong capability and clever resourcefulness.
translations.idiomatic: That is proof of his force and cleverness.

sentences.zh: 公忠之道，亦在其中矣。

translations.literal: The way of public loyalty was also within it.
translations.idiomatic: Public loyalty was part of it as well.

sentences.zh: 不然，則何以致是哉！

translations.literal: Otherwise, how could he have brought this about!
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, how could he have achieved such things!

sentences.zh: 若使昭德用謙御下，以柔守剛，不恃專權，常能寡過，則復皇嗣而非晚，保臣節而必終。

translations.literal: If Zhaode had used humility to govern subordinates, used softness to keep firmness, not relied on monopoly of power, and always been able to have few faults, then restoring the imperial heir would not have been late, and preserving ministerial integrity he would surely have ended well.
translations.idiomatic: Had Zhaode governed subordinates with humility, tempered firmness with softness, not relied on monopoly of power, and kept his faults few, he could have restored the heir without delay and preserved his integrity to the end.

sentences.zh: 蓋由道乏弘持，器難苞貯，純剛是失，卷智不全。

translations.literal: It was because the Way lacked broad sustaining, his vessel was hard to contain, pure firmness was his fault, and rolled-up wisdom was not complete.
translations.idiomatic: But his way lacked breadth, his vessel could not hold all, pure stubbornness was his flaw, and he did not fully restrain his wit.

sentences.zh: 所以丘愔抗陳，鄧注深論，瓦解而固難收拾，風摧而豈易扶持。

translations.literal: Therefore Qiu Yin remonstrated boldly and Deng Zhu argued deeply; once dissolved it was truly hard to gather up, once the wind struck it was how easily supported?
translations.idiomatic: Hence Qiu Yin's bold memorial and Deng Zhu's deep treatise—once he crumbled he was hard to salvage, once the wind struck him he could not easily be propped up.

sentences.zh: 自取誅夷，人誰怨懟？

translations.literal: He brought execution upon himself—who would resent and complain?
translations.idiomatic: He brought execution on himself—who could blame others?

sentences.zh: 讚曰：政無刑法，時屬艱危。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Government lacked penal law; the times belonged to hardship and peril.
translations.idiomatic: Encomium: Government lacked firm law; the times were perilous.

sentences.zh: 裴炎之智，慮淺見遲。

translations.literal: Pei Yan's wisdom was shallow in counsel and slow in sight.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yan's wisdom was shallow and slow.

sentences.zh: 禕之履行，貸色自欺。

translations.literal: Yizhi's conduct lent color to self-deception.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhi's conduct lent color to self-delusion.

sentences.zh: 昭德強猛，何由不虧？

translations.literal: Zhaode was strong and fierce—how could he not come to loss?
translations.idiomatic: Zhaode was fierce and forceful—how could he not come to ruin?

sentences.zh: 死無令譽，孰謂非宜。

translations.literal: Death without fair reputation—who would say it was not fitting?
translations.idiomatic: Death without fair fame—who would call that unjust?

sentences.zh: 玄同不幸，顛殞亦隨。

translations.literal: Xuantong was unfortunate; toppling death followed as well.
translations.idiomatic: Xuantong was unfortunate, and ruin followed in his wake.
